The Storyteller makes it true unless it would directly defeat a major character.

From "Peoples of the Known World" by Liris Kant, Third Chair of Natural Philosophy, Monsera University Hyumans live on every continent. They are not the strongest, longest lived, or most magically gifted heritage. What they have is adaptability. Placed in a difficult environment, Hyuman communities typically build permanent settlements within two generations and regard the land as their own within four. Regional differences among Hyumans are larger than in most heritages, so I record them by origin. Asura Kingdom: the wealthiest and most culturally dominant Hyuman nation. Its people tend to assume their customs are the standard, usually without arrogance, simply because they have never had reason to question it. Three Magic Kingdoms: the north produces scholars, researchers, and engineers. Most northerners I interviewed had a specific subject of study and discussed it readily. Biheiril: a remote kingdom bordered by mountains and old forest. Its people are quieter than most. They share their land with the Superd and keep long standing ties with the Ogres of the nearby islands. Holy Land of Swords: children train in swordsmanship from early childhood. Adults hold strong, detailed opinions on technique. Holy Kingdom of Milishion: one of the most religious societies in the world, with many historical sites. For generations it was the wall between demons and Hyumans. It is more integrated now than in the past. Monsera: raised in a city where every heritage and culture lives within walking distance. Monserans resist easy classification. Strife Zone: tough, pragmatic, and distrustful of authority. They learn early that no one will provide for them. Breakwater: as self reliant as Strife Zone Hyumans, but softened by a local custom of minding one's own business while still helping neighbors. Corporate Kingdoms: the few who leave describe freedom as something they never had before, and they treat it with unusual care.

Average Lifespan: 100 years. Innate Attribute: Any single attribute of the player's choice. Starts at 2 dots, maximum raised by 1 beyond column cap. Note Innate on sheet. Innate Flaw - Restless: If the character does not act meaningfully on at least one Driving Factor per story arc, roll Willpower dots at the arc's end. Each failure deals 1 Sanity damage. Attribute Flaw: None. Hyumans may place any attribute group in their Affinity column. Heritage Merit (choose 1, record in Merits, Flaws, and Backgrounds section): Hyuman Adaptability: Grants a 5-5-5 attribute spread instead of the standard Affinity/Standard/Aversion designation. Tenacity: A dotted merit. Whenever the character regains Willpower, they regain 1 additional point for each dot in this merit.

Hyumans have no single inherited magic of their own. What they have instead is the thing Liris Kant spends most of her entry trying to name: an ability to take whatever the world hands them and make it theirs. A Hyuman character's free Heritage magic dot goes to one of the following. The Heritage magic of a non-Hyuman parent. The character awakens that parent's bloodline magic and raises it with XP from then on. Unlike other heritages, a Hyuman is never locked out of a spell. Each new dot grants one of that rank's two spells for free, and the other can be bought with XP at the same cost as buying a spell in any other magic. 1 dot in any casting school (Fire, Water, Air, Earth, Nature, Bright, or Shade). 1 dot in any circle magic. Whichever is chosen, a Hyuman receives one free dot and no more.

From "Peoples of the Known World" by Liris Kant, Third Chair of Natural Philosophy, Monsera University I have met Badigadi twice. His title, Demon King of Wisdom and Wine, is accurate. He has six arms, but most people notice his presence and his laugh first. The Immortal Mix are Badigadi's descendants. Every four armed demon on the Demon Continent traces their line to him. There are more of them than one might expect from a single ancestor. He has lived a very long time, and his wife Kishirika, the Immortal Demon King who distributes the Eyes of God, has died and reincarnated at least five times, leaving him long stretches alone. He has not spent them in restraint. Four arms mark a descendant no matter how many generations removed. When a four armed child is born to parents with two arms, the family learns something about its history. The Immortal Mix treat this with good humor. They are tall, well above most Hyumans. Their four arms are fully functional, and trained fighters among them are formidable. Magic is their weakness. Badigadi has little magical aptitude, and neither, as a rule, do his descendants. They live about four hundred years. The four arms persist through the generations. The immortality does not. Badigadi does not seem troubled by this.

Average Lifespan: 400 years. Innate Attribute (choose 1, note Innate on sheet): Strength: For a character whose four-armed physical power and raw combat capability define them. Dexterity: For a character whose four-armed coordination and combat versatility define them. Innate Flaw - Badi's Blood: The Immortal Demon King Badigadi is renowned for many things. Magical aptitude is not among them. His descendants share this limitation. Immortal Mix demons suffer a 1 die penalty on all Magic ability rolls. Attribute Flaw - Mental: Mental attributes cannot be your Affinity column. They can only be your Standard or Aversion column. Physical Note: Every Immortal Mix demon with four arms can trace their lineage back to Badigadi, the six-armed Immortal Demon King of the Demon Continent. Heritage Merit (choose 1, record in Merits, Flaws, and Backgrounds section): Four Armed Fighting: As long as you are not wielding a weapon you may make one additional Martial Arts attack per turn. Wielding a weapon requires enough fine motor coordination across four arms that your other arms hang back rather than risk harming yourself. Quadbidextrous: When wielding a melee weapon you may grip it with multiple hands. Each hand gripping the weapon beyond the first adds 1 bonus die to damage rolls. The weapon must be long enough for all hands to grasp simultaneously such as a polearm, nagamaki, or claymore. Cannot be combined with Four Armed Fighting.
Badigadi does not stay hurt, and neither do his descendants. Undying Flesh is the inherited regeneration of the Immortal Demon Kings.

Mana Cost: 1 or more (see Effect) Speed: Instant, Downtime Type: Healing Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: 1 die per mana spent, up to your Undying Flesh dots or Max Mana Per Turn, whichever comes first Defense: None Effect: During your Upkeep Phase, spend at least 1 mana. Roll 1 die for each mana spent, up to your Heritage dots or Max Mana Per Turn, whichever comes first. Each success heals using the healing tier your rank allows. Outside combat you may simply heal up based on your dots in this Heritage magic. Undying Flesh has no Option A or Option B. It is a single spell and each rank improves what it can heal. Rank Heals 1 Core Basic healing. 2 Terrestrial Instead of using a success for Basic healing, you can spend it to end one condition affecting you, such as Bleeding or Burning. 3 Aerial Advanced healing. 4 Lunar During downtime, you can use Master healing once a day to regenerate a lost limb. 5 Stellar Expert healing. 6 Galactic Master healing, even in combat. 7 Cosmic Resurrection. After death, during downtime, you may cast Resurrection on your own body once per day while its mana countdown lasts, spending mana from what the body has left. If the roll succeeds, you resurrect. If it fails and the body has no mana left, you are permanently dead. This does not work if you chose to die (Blaze of Glory).

From "Peoples of the Known World" by Liris Kant, Third Chair of Natural Philosophy, Monsera University Before I visited Ogre Island I had read older scholarly accounts that focused on the Ogres' size and capacity for violence. Those accounts were wrong, and I believed them anyway. I note this because the error is easy to make. Ogres live on Ogre Island, an archipelago off the northeastern coast of the Central Continent. Their ancestors left the Demon Continent during a period of constant war. They did not want to fight. They wanted to train, argue, and live in peace, so they left. Their alliance with the Hyumans of Biheiril began with a rescue. Ancient Ogres pulled a crew of Biheiril sailors out of the sea, including someone of importance whose identity changes with the telling. The two peoples have been close ever since. Ogres vary widely in appearance. Some are nearly Hyuman in proportion, with skin in shades of red, green, blue, or pink. Others are massive, closer to a minotaur in build. All have horns, ranging from small bumps to long sweeping structures. Size and build do not follow gender. In Ogre courtship, beautiful Ogres are usually drawn to ugly ones and ugly ones to beautiful ones. There are exceptions, but the pattern is strong. The most striking Ogre I met was happily partnered with someone best described as magnificently grotesque. Ogre culture is monastic in the sense of disciplined self development, not withdrawal. They practice martial traditions ranging from striking styles to grappling and pursue them with both seriousness and enjoyment. They also eat well, drink often, and argue about everything. Their pubs are the loudest I have encountered. Tables are struck for emphasis and voices reach volumes I would associate with emergencies. On my first night, two Ogres stood and faced each other across a table, and I expected a fight. They were debating grappling techniques. It ended with both laughing and refilling each other's cups. An adult Ogre who throws the first punch is exiled. To an Ogre, arguing is not fighting and a raised voice is not a raised hand. They hold this line consistently. Children who lash out are taught patiently rather than punished. During my stay I saw no exile, because no adult broke the rule. Ogres will defend themselves, their friends, and strangers with everything they have. Most say they would die for someone they had never met, and they say it as a plain statement of fact. They accept formal duels, fight them honorably, and end them without killing whenever possible.

Average Lifespan: 200 years. Innate Attribute (choose 1, note Innate on sheet): Strength: For a character whose physical power and imposing presence define them. Wisdom: For a character whose monastic discipline and focused mind define them. Innate Flaw - Ogre's Grace: An Ogre or Oni cannot willingly initiate a confrontation they believe will end in physical violence. They may argue, debate, and negotiate freely. They may accept a duel if one is formally suggested by the other party. But throwing the first punch means exile from their tribe and lasting reputation damage among their people. Attribute Flaw - Social: Social attributes cannot be your Affinity column. They can only be your Standard or Aversion column. Heritage Merit (choose 1, record in Merits, Flaws, and Backgrounds section): Iron Gut: Grants a free specialty in Endurance called Iron Gut, providing a bonus die on Endurance rolls against poison, toxins, and ingested or inhaled hazards. Peacemaker: Grants a free specialty in Diplomacy called Peacemaker, providing a bonus die on Diplomacy rolls when attempting to de-escalate conflict, negotiate terms, or find common ground before a situation turns violent.

Ogre law forbids throwing the first blow, so their inherited magic never learned how. Oni Ward is defense and protection: a body that will not break, a stance that shelters others, and a presence that talks a fight down before it starts. No Oni Ward spell can start a fight. Spells that strike back only work against someone who has already attacked. Primary: Wisdom + Endurance + Oni Ward Secondary: Composure + Diplomacy + Oni Ward Extra mana: Attack or damage. 1 die per mana, up to your Oni Ward dots or Max Mana Per Turn, whichever comes first.

Mana Cost: 1 Speed: Reaction Type: Defense Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: Wisdom + Endurance + Oni Ward Defense: None Effect: When you are attacked, roll your dice pool. Each success removes 1 success from the attacker's roll.

Mana Cost: 1, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Enhancement, Attuned Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: Composure + Diplomacy + Oni Ward Defense: None Effect: While attuned, add your Heritage dots to Diplomacy rolls made to de-escalate a situation before violence begins.

Mana Cost: 2, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Defense, Attuned Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: Wisdom + Endurance + Oni Ward Defense: None Effect: While attuned, add half your Heritage dots, rounded up, to your BDT.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Reaction Type: Attack Use: Combat Range: Melee, against the creature that hit you Dice Pool: Wisdom + Endurance + Oni Ward Defense: Target's choice of defense Effect: After an attack hits you, make one unarmed or weapon attack against that attacker with this dice pool at no AP cost.

Mana Cost: 3 Speed: Reaction Type: Defense Use: Combat Range: One ally in an adjacent zone Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: An attack aimed at the ally hits you instead. You defend against it normally.

Mana Cost: 3 Speed: Instant Type: Debuff Use: Combat Range: Melee, one creature that has attacked this scene Dice Pool: Wisdom + Endurance + Oni Ward Defense: Strength + Athletics, then Strength + Athletics to break free Effect: The target resists with Strength + Athletics. If you beat them, they are restrained and cannot attack until they beat your successes with Strength + Athletics on their turn.

Mana Cost: 4, upkeep 3 each Upkeep Phase Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Defense, Persistent Use: Combat Range: Allies in adjacent zones Dice Pool: Wisdom + Endurance + Oni Ward Defense: None Effect: While maintained, allies in adjacent zones add half your Heritage dots, rounded up, to their BDT.

Mana Cost: 4, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Defense, Attuned Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, if you have not moved this turn, you cannot be moved, knocked prone, or Rooted.

Mana Cost: 5, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Enhancement, Attuned Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, ignore wound penalties from Bashing and Lethal damage.

Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Reaction Type: Defense Use: Combat Range: Self or one ally in an adjacent zone Dice Pool: Wisdom + Endurance + Oni Ward Defense: Strength + Athletics Effect: When a melee attack against you or an ally in an adjacent zone fails, roll your dice pool. The attacker resists with Strength + Athletics. If you beat them, they drop their weapon.

Mana Cost: 6, upkeep 5 each Upkeep Phase Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Defense, Persistent Use: Combat Range: One ally in sight Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While maintained, the first attack that hits the ally each turn deals them no damage. You take half of it instead, rounded down.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Instant Type: Debuff Use: Combat Range: All adjacent zones Dice Pool: Composure + Diplomacy + Oni Ward Defense: Composure + Diplomacy Effect: Every creature in range resists with Composure + Diplomacy. Each one you beat cannot attack on their next turn.

Mana Cost: 7, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Defense, Attuned Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, every hit against you is treated as one damage threshold lower: Aggravated becomes Lethal, Lethal becomes Bashing, and Bashing deals nothing.

Mana Cost: 7, upkeep 6 each Upkeep Phase Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Persistent Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Up to 6 connected zones in sight Dice Pool: Composure + Diplomacy + Oni Ward Defense: Willpower Effect: Roll when cast. While maintained, anyone who tries to attack inside those zones must first beat your successes with Willpower. On a failure the action is wasted.

Yuan-Ti, Lizardfolk, Dragonewt, Thri-Kreen, Aranea, and similar. Cold blooded and ancient. From Liris Kant's entry on the monster peoples The Reptilian and Bug peoples range from the Yuan-Ti to the Thri-Kreen and the Aranea. They are cold blooded, so their energy depends on the temperature. At the right temperature they are as active as anyone. In the cold they slow down, know it, and plan around it. Their communities favor hierarchy and tradition, and those structures have stayed stable because they work. They are slow to get to know and worth the time.

Average Lifespan: 200 years for Reptilian types, 100 years for Bug types. Innate Attribute (choose 1, note Innate on sheet): Fortitude: For a character whose natural resilience and physical toughness define them. Perception: For a character whose sharp senses and environmental awareness define them. Innate Flaw - Cold Blooded: Reptilian and Bug monsters suffer a penalty die on all rolls made in extreme cold environments. Attribute Flaw - Social: Social attributes cannot be your Affinity column. They can only be your Standard or Aversion column. Heritage Merit (choose 1, record in Merits, Flaws, and Backgrounds section): Scaled Hide: Grants a free specialty in Endurance called Scaled Hide, providing a bonus die against physical damage reflecting their natural armor. Toxic Knack: Grants a free specialty in a magic ability of the player's choice with Storyteller approval, reflecting an innate toxic, chemical, or biological production unique to their creature type.

Fangs, stingers, glands, and spit. Venom is the toxic gift shared by the cold blooded and many legged peoples of Monsera. Each species carries a different poison, and every one of them can be refined. Primary: Dexterity + Martial Arts + Venom Secondary: Intelligence + Alchemy + Venom Extra mana: Damage only. 1 die per mana, up to your Venom dots or Max Mana Per Turn, whichever comes first. Poisoned (condition): the target takes 1 Bashing damage during their Upkeep Phase for a number of turns equal to the mana spent on the spell that applied it. Poisoned ends early through Detoxification or Bright Magic.

Mana Cost: 1 Speed: Instant Type: Attack Use: Combat Range: Melee Dice Pool: Dexterity + Martial Arts + Venom Defense: Target's choice of defense Effect: Attack with your natural weapons. On a hit the target gains the Poisoned condition.

Mana Cost: 1, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Enhancement, Attuned Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: Intelligence + Alchemy + Venom Defense: None Effect: While attuned, add your Heritage dots to Awareness and Survival rolls to track by scent and to detect poisons.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Instant Type: Attack Use: Combat Range: One target in an adjacent zone Dice Pool: Dexterity + Martial Arts + Venom Defense: Target's choice of defense Effect: On a hit the target suffers -2 dice on sight-based rolls on their next turn instead of taking damage.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Outside combat only Range: Self Dice Pool: Intelligence + Alchemy + Venom Defense: None Effect: Over a scene, milk doses of your venom equal to your successes, up to your Heritage dots. Doses keep for one session. A weapon coated with a dose applies the Poisoned condition on its next hit.

Mana Cost: 3 Speed: Instant Type: Attack Use: Combat Range: Melee Dice Pool: Dexterity + Martial Arts + Venom Defense: Target's choice of defense Effect: Venom Bite whose hit also costs the target 1 AP on their next turn.

Mana Cost: 3, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Defense, Attuned Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: Fortitude + Endurance + Venom Defense: None Effect: While attuned, resist poisons with this dice pool.

Mana Cost: 4 Speed: Instant Type: Attack Use: Combat Range: Melee Dice Pool: Dexterity + Martial Arts + Venom Defense: Target's choice of defense Effect: Venom Bite whose Poisoned damage is Lethal instead of Bashing.

Mana Cost: 4 Speed: Instant Type: Debuff Use: Combat Range: One target in an adjacent zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Alchemy + Venom Defense: Dexterity + Athletics, then Strength + Athletics to break free Effect: The target resists with Dexterity + Athletics. If you beat them, they gain the Rooted condition until they beat your successes with Strength + Athletics on their turn.

Mana Cost: 5, upkeep 4 each Upkeep Phase Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Attack, Persistent Use: Combat Range: One zone in sight Dice Pool: Dexterity + Martial Arts + Venom Defense: Fortitude + Endurance, which reduces the damage value Effect: Roll when cast. Successes plus mana spent set the damage value. Anyone who enters or begins their turn in the zone rolls Fortitude + Endurance; their successes reduce the damage value, and the rest is compared against their damage thresholds.
Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Reaction Type: Healing Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: Once per scene, shed your outer layer. Remove all conditions and heal 1 Lethal damage.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Instant Type: Attack Use: Combat Range: Melee Dice Pool: Dexterity + Martial Arts + Venom Defense: Target's choice of defense Effect: Venom Bite whose target gains the Bleeding condition as well as Poisoned.

Mana Cost: 6, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Enhancement, Attuned Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, each Venom Bite hit also applies your choice of -2 dice on the target's next roll, the loss of 1 AP, or the Bleeding condition.

Mana Cost: 7 Speed: Instant Type: Attack Use: Combat Range: Melee Dice Pool: Dexterity + Martial Arts + Venom Defense: Target's choice of defense, then Fortitude + Endurance Effect: On a hit, the target also resists with Fortitude + Endurance. If you beat them, the hit is treated as meeting the next-higher damage threshold, and Poisoned lasts the whole scene.

Mana Cost: 7, upkeep 6 each Upkeep Phase Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Attack, Persistent Use: Combat Range: Up to 6 connected zones around you Dice Pool: Dexterity + Martial Arts + Venom Defense: Fortitude + Endurance, which reduces the damage value Effect: Toxic Cloud across up to 6 connected zones. It moves with you during each Upkeep Phase and never affects your allies.

Every heritage in this part requires Storyteller approval before character creation. A character of a Rare Heritage will turn heads in most places they go, and the Storyteller should be ready to make that part of the story. Storyteller Note: It is not recommended to let two or more players play the same Rare Heritage, unless you are running a specific kind of game, such as an all werewolf or all vampire campaign.

Six Monster sub-types are rare outside the deep pockets of Monsera and the Shaded Isles. They are listed alphabetically in this part, marked Monster Faction. Liris Kant's introduction to the monster peoples appears under Monster Factions at the start of Part 1. Incorporeal Undead cannot be chosen at character creation; their entry explains how a character becomes one.

Liches, Dullahan, Skeletons, Prometheans, and similar. Corporeal Undead sustain themselves through mana rather than conventional biological processes. Functionally immortal as long as mana is maintained. From Liris Kant's entry on the monster peoples The Corporeal Undead are liches, dullahans, skeletons, prometheans, and others sustained by mana rather than biology. Most live in the Shaded Isles, though some live in Monsera proper. Three ancient noble houses have ruled the isles for longer than most records go back: one led by a vampire, one by a lich, and one by a dullahan. The isles joined the Monsera kingdom a generation ago while keeping their own internal government. The transition went more smoothly than expected, largely because the Slime King was both respectful and clear about his terms. The permanent storm over the isles was designed by a lich and remains in place.

Average Lifespan: Immortal, as long as mana is maintained. Innate Attribute (choose 1, note Innate on sheet): Intelligence: For a character whose ancient accumulated knowledge and sharp analytical mind define them. Composure: For a character whose unshakeable stillness and emotional detachment define them. Innate Flaw - Mana Dependent: Corporeal Undead who fully deplete their mana and remain at zero for an extended period begin to deteriorate physically. Each session spent at zero mana deals 1 Aggravated damage that cannot be healed until mana is restored. Attribute Flaw - Physical: Physical attributes cannot be your Affinity column. They can only be your Standard or Aversion column. Heritage Merit (choose 1, record in Merits, Flaws, and Backgrounds section): Undying Resilience: Grants a free specialty in Endurance called Undying, providing a bonus die against poison, disease, and environmental hazards that affect living tissue. Death Sense: Grants a free specialty in Awareness called Death Sense, providing a bonus die on Awareness rolls to detect the presence of death, undead creatures, or necrotic magic in the surrounding area.

The Corporeal Undead are held together by mana rather than breath. Deathless is the control they have over that state: a body that feels nothing, rebuilds itself from mana, and refuses to stay down. Primary: Composure + Endurance + Deathless Secondary: Intelligence + Attunement + Deathless Extra mana: Attack or damage. 1 die per mana, up to your Deathless dots or Max Mana Per Turn, whichever comes first.

Mana Cost: 1, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Enhancement, Attuned Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, ignore wound penalties from Bashing damage.

Mana Cost: 1, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Attuned Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: Composure + Endurance + Deathless Defense: Perception + Awareness Effect: Roll when you attune. While attuned you appear fully dead. Seeing through it requires beating your successes with Perception + Awareness.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Instant Type: Healing Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: Composure + Endurance + Deathless Defense: None Effect: Cast during your Upkeep Phase. Basic healing on yourself.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Instant Type: Attack Use: Combat Range: Touch Dice Pool: Composure + Endurance + Deathless Defense: Target's choice of defense Effect: On a hit, the target also gains the Chilled condition.

Mana Cost: 3, upkeep 2 each Upkeep Phase Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Persistent Use: Combat and outside combat Range: An adjacent zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Attunement + Deathless Defense: None Effect: A hand, head, or other part of you detaches and acts on its own in an adjacent zone to scout or carry something small. You perceive through it.

Mana Cost: 3, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Defense, Attuned Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, you are immune to suffocation, airborne poisons, and disease.

Mana Cost: 4 Speed: Instant Type: Healing Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: Composure + Endurance + Deathless Defense: None Effect: Cast during your Upkeep Phase. Advanced healing on yourself.

Mana Cost: 4, upkeep 3 each Upkeep Phase Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Debuff, Persistent Use: Combat Range: All adjacent zones Dice Pool: Composure + Endurance + Deathless Defense: Composure + Presence Effect: Each enemy in range resists with Composure + Presence when it is cast. Each one you beat suffers -2 dice to attack you while maintained.

Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Reaction Type: Defense Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: Once per scene, when a hit would make you Incapacitated, you collapse instead and reform in an adjacent zone at your next Upkeep Phase without that hit's damage.

Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Instant Type: Attack Use: Combat Range: Touch Dice Pool: Composure + Endurance + Deathless Defense: Target's choice of defense Effect: On a hit, regain mana equal to the boxes of damage dealt.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Outside combat only Range: Touch Dice Pool: Intelligence + Attunement + Deathless Defense: None Effect: Over a session of work, bind your existence to one object. While it exists, your death ends with you reforming beside it after one day.

Mana Cost: 6, upkeep 5 each Upkeep Phase Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Persistent Use: Combat Range: Mindless undead in sight Dice Pool: Composure + Endurance + Deathless Defense: None for mindless undead; undead imprinted by another necromancer or lich roll their controller's dice pool Effect: Mindless undead in sight, up to your Heritage dots in number, obey you while maintained. Undead imprinted by another necromancer or lich resist with their controller's dice pool.

Mana Cost: 7, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Defense, Attuned Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, damage cannot take you past Incapacitated. Bright Magic ignores this protection.

Mana Cost: 7, upkeep 6 each Upkeep Phase Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Conjuration, Persistent Use: Combat Range: Corpses or skeletons in sight Dice Pool: Composure + Endurance + Deathless Defense: Target's choice of defense against its attacks Effect: Raise up to your Heritage dots in bodies as one conjuration. During each Upkeep Phase, each risen body may move one zone or attack one enemy in a zone adjacent to it using your dice pool.

From "Peoples of the Known World" by Liris Kant, Third Chair of Natural Philosophy, Monsera University The Demon Continent holds more peoples than any survey could count. Every valley, bog, and mountain pass seems to have its own tribe, and no two look alike. I have met demons with horns and demons with none, demons with skin of every color, demons with extra eyes, tails, or wings, and one small fellow whose face I never once saw beneath the brim of his hat. The continent's high ambient mana seems to push each bloodline in its own direction. These are the ordinary demons of the continent. They are not the Immortal Demon Kings, not the Immortal Mix descended from Badigadi's line, and not the bestial peoples counted among the monster factions. Most live about two hundred years. Outside the Demon Continent they are still an unusual sight, though Monsera's ports see more of them every year. The tribes differ so widely that I will not pretend to describe them all. Each carries its own gifts, its own weaknesses, and its own quiet magic in the blood.

Building a Demon: A Demon character is built by the player and the Storyteller together. Decide on the character's tribe and look first, then use that picture to choose the Innate Attribute, Innate Flaw, Attribute Flaw, and Heritage magic below. Average Lifespan: 200 years. Innate Attribute: Chosen with the Storyteller to fit the character's tribe. Starts at 2 dots, maximum raised by 1 beyond the column cap. Note Innate on sheet. Innate Flaw: Chosen with the Storyteller to fit the character's tribe. Like every Innate Flaw, it grants no extra dots. It should be about as much of a drawback as the other heritages' Innate Flaws, such as a penalty die on one kind of roll. Attribute Flaw: Chosen with the Storyteller. One column (Physical, Social, or Mental) can never be your Affinity column; it can only be your Standard or Aversion column. A frail tribe of spellcasters, for example, would take Physical. Heritage Merit (choose 1, record in Merits, Flaws, and Backgrounds section): Tribal Gift: Grants a free specialty in one ability chosen with the Storyteller that reflects your tribe's nature, providing a bonus die when that gift applies. Demon Tongue: Grants a free specialty in Diplomacy called Demon Tongue, providing a bonus die on rolls to deal with the tribes, domains, and Demon Kings of the Demon Continent. Mana Born: Grants a free specialty in Attunement called Mana Born, providing a bonus die on rolls to sense dense ambient mana and to resist mana sickness.

Every demon tribe carries its own magic in the blood. A Demon's Heritage magic is designed by the player and the Storyteller together around the tribe's nature, and it follows every rule for Heritage magic in this chapter. Use these guidelines when building it. Name: Give the magic a name that fits the tribe. Pools: Choose a Primary and a Secondary dice pool, each Attribute + Ability + your Heritage dots, like every other Heritage magic. Ranks: Seven ranks, Core through Cosmic. Each rank offers an Option A and an Option B spell, and the choice is permanent. Mana: Every spell costs mana equal to its rank. Upkeep is always the cost minus 1, so no Core spell can be persistent. Balance: Use the other Heritage magics in this chapter as a measuring stick. Rank 1 spells have no lasting effects in combat, and power should rise evenly from rank to rank. Pacing: The Storyteller may write the spells one rank at a time, as the character awakens each new dot, rather than all seven at creation.

From "Peoples of the Known World" by Liris Kant, Third Chair of Natural Philosophy, Monsera University I have a personal stake in this entry. I was one of the first scholars outside Monsera to write about the devils settling on Floor 15 of The Dungeon. That article drew more correspondence than anything else I have published, and most of it came from people who had never met a devil. Devils are widely misunderstood, and the difficulty is that the common beliefs are not entirely false. They do harvest mana from the emotions of those around them. Hell has been a place of real suffering. What the reputation leaves out is that a people is not a single person, and the history of some devils does not predict the behavior of the one in front of you. Devils can regenerate mana from any emotion, not only suffering. The Immortal Devil Queen Sciel credits this discovery to her conversations with the Slime King about sixty years ago. If a devil can live on joy as easily as misery, there is no longer any reason to cause misery. Not all devils accept this. Zagan controls four levels of Hell and holds the Duchess Gremory prisoner. Marchosias fights beside him by choice. Most of the devils who reject Zagan's view now live in Nite City on Floor 15 of The Dungeon. It is a city where nearly everything is legal and cheap, where currency is often emotional rather than financial, and where seven districts correspond to the seven emotional affinities. Sciel was Nite City's first mayor and held the post until the city could govern itself. Since then she has traveled as an envoy with the Slime King's authority, arguing that devils deserve to exist without proving it every day. She writes books and appears on Crystalz programs. We exchange manuscripts before publication, and her notes on mine are always correct. Hell has nine levels. Level 9 is the entry point for the banished. Level 1 is the deepest, where Lucifer holds court. Each level is ruled by a prince, princess, duke, or duchess. Zagan has been conquering levels and claiming them for himself. Lucifer has responded with restraint. He cares for the devils, Hyumans, and others in Hell in his own way, and his anti authoritarian philosophy makes simply ordering Zagan to stop feel inconsistent to him. Hell is at a stalemate. Belethore, Lucifer's son and Sciel's former betrothed, was killed and reincarnated into an ordinary devil family with his memories and most of his power intact. He now goes by Mahk and recently took over Level 14 3/4 Studios, between Floors 14 and 15 of The Dungeon. His shows feature devils alongside people of every heritage, slowly making them ordinary in the public eye. I am often asked whether devils can be trusted. It is not a question anyone asks about Elves or Dwarves, and it assumes a uniformity that does not exist. The devils I know have been exactly as trustworthy as everyone else I know. It depends on the individual. A devil's skin color shows their emotional affinity. The Aceditia (Sloth and Diligence) are blue and gray. The Iracunditia (Wrath and Patience) are deep red and black. The Gulanitia (Gluttony and Temperance) are amber and burnt orange. The Vanitia (Pride and Humility) are bronze and copper. The Inviditia (Envy and Kindness) are green and teal. The Carnavitia (Lust and Chastity) are violet and soft pink. The Avaritia (Greed and Charity) are gold and alabaster. Immortal devils show a single solid color. Their descendants carry both colors of their type in a pattern unique to each individual. Skin color tells you a devil's affinity. It does not tell you their character.

Average Lifespan: 400 years. Immortal Devils are Immortal. Devil Spawn are Fey Touched and live 400 years. Innate Attribute (choose 1, note Innate on sheet): Intelligence: For a character whose magical aptitude and contractual cunning define them. Charisma: For a character whose emotional attunement and social presence define them. Innate Flaw - Devil's Rejects: Devils suffer a 1 die penalty on Persuasion rolls when attempting to convince others of their genuine intentions. The reputation of their kind precedes them in almost every corner of Terrana, especially outside of Monsera and Nite City. Attribute Flaw - Physical: Physical attributes cannot be your Affinity column. They can only be your Standard or Aversion column. Wings: Almost every devil has wings, though they vary widely in size and usefulness. Some are strong enough for true flight, and some are only for show. Every devil can glide when falling, provided there is room to spread their wings, whether or not they can truly fly. Devil Type: Choose one of the seven devil types at creation. Your type determines your Emotional Affinity and your skin color combination. Devils can harvest mana from any emotion around them, but harvest more from the Virtue or Vice of their calibration and are naturally drawn to people exhibiting those emotions. Devil Type Scale Primary Color Secondary Color Aceditia Sloth/Diligence Blue Gray Iracunditia Wrath/Patience Deep Red Black Gulanitia Gluttony/Temperance Amber Burnt Orange Vanitia Pride/Humility Bronze Copper Inviditia Envy/Kindness Green Teal Carnavitia Lust/Chastity Violet Soft Pink Avaritia Greed/Charity Gold Alabaster Heritage Merit (choose 1, record in Merits, Flaws, and Backgrounds section): Devil Wings: Your wings are strong enough for true flight. Grants a free specialty in Athletics called Flight, providing a bonus die on Athletics rolls made while flying. Without this merit a devil can still glide, but cannot gain altitude. Emotional Taste: A dotted merit. During combat, if anyone within a number of zones equal to your dots in this merit is showing a strong emotion tied to your Devil Type, you may gain 1 additional mana during your Upkeep Phase. You can do this a number of times per combat equal to your dots in this merit. Emotional Harvest: Whenever you would regain mana through any means you regain double that amount instead. Devil Spawn: Available only if one parent is a non-devil heritage. You may choose one merit from that heritage instead of the options listed here. Devil Spawn are Fey Touched (see Fey Touched at the start of this chapter).

Contract Magic is a circle magic. Anyone in Terrana can learn it, though few bother, and devils are the only people born with it. Like all circle magic, a contract can only be written outside combat, and the mana is spent when it is written. A finished contract can be carried and signed at any time, in combat or social combat included. A contract binds only those who sign it willingly unless a spell says otherwise, and its terms take effect the moment it is signed. Primary: Intelligence + Circle Magic + Contract Magic Secondary: Charisma + Persuasion + Contract Magic Extra mana: Writing roll only. 1 die per mana, up to your Contract Magic dots or Max Mana Per Turn, whichever comes first.

Mana Cost: 1, spent when written Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Written outside combat; the finished contract can be used any time Range: Signers Dice Pool: Intelligence + Circle Magic + Contract Magic Defense: None Effect: A contract holding one simple promise between two signers. Both know at once if it is broken.

Mana Cost: 1, spent when written Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Written outside combat; the finished contract can be used any time Range: One document Dice Pool: Intelligence + Circle Magic + Contract Magic Defense: None Effect: Seal an existing agreement or document. Whoever reads it adds your successes as bonus dice to rolls to find loopholes, lies, and hidden clauses in it.

Mana Cost: 2, spent when written Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Written outside combat; the finished contract can be used any time Range: Signers Dice Pool: Intelligence + Circle Magic + Contract Magic Defense: None Effect: A signer gives you 1 mana or 1 Willpower when they sign, in exchange for a favor named in the contract. If you fail to deliver the favor, you take 1 Lethal damage.

Mana Cost: 2, spent when written Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Written outside combat; the finished contract can be used any time Range: Signers Dice Pool: Charisma + Persuasion + Contract Magic Defense: None Effect: The contract records how each signer felt when they signed. Whoever holds it knows if any signer felt fear, deceit, or anger at that moment.

Mana Cost: 3, spent when written Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Written outside combat; the finished contract can be used any time Range: Signers Dice Pool: Intelligence + Circle Magic + Contract Magic Defense: None Effect: Whoever breaks the contract takes Bashing damage equal to your successes when writing it, up to your Heritage dots.

Mana Cost: 3, spent when written Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Written outside combat; the finished contract can be used any time Range: One zone or room Dice Pool: Intelligence + Circle Magic + Contract Magic Defense: None Effect: Draw a circle around a room or zone. For the next scene held inside it, anyone who lies suffers -2 dice for that scene, and everyone in the circle knows a lie was told.

Mana Cost: 4, spent when written Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Written outside combat; the finished contract can be used any time Range: Signers Dice Pool: Intelligence + Circle Magic + Contract Magic Defense: None Effect: While a signer owes you under the contract, they cannot hide their location from you and suffer -2 dice to attack you.

Mana Cost: 4, spent when written Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Written outside combat; the finished contract can be used any time Range: Signers Dice Pool: Charisma + Persuasion + Contract Magic Defense: None Effect: For one session after signing, signers may split damage they take with another signer, half each, rounded in favor of the one hit.

Mana Cost: 5, spent when written Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Written outside combat; the finished contract can be used any time Range: Signers Dice Pool: Intelligence + Circle Magic + Contract Magic Defense: None Effect: Penalty Clause whose damage is Lethal.

Mana Cost: 5, spent when written Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Written outside combat; the finished contract can be used any time Range: Signers Dice Pool: Charisma + Persuasion + Contract Magic Defense: None Effect: When you call in the debt, a signer must perform one task within their ability. Refusing triggers the contract's penalty.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Outside combat only Range: One contract or magical agreement Dice Pool: Intelligence + Circle Magic + Contract Magic Defense: The contract's original writing successes Effect: Study a contract or magical agreement over a scene. Roll against its maker's writing successes. If you win, you may void it.

Mana Cost: 6, spent when written Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Written outside combat; the finished contract can be used any time Range: Whoever accepts the gift Dice Pool: Charisma + Persuasion + Contract Magic Defense: Willpower Effect: Write a contract into a gift: a drink, a token, a pair of gloves. Whoever accepts it is bound to one condition you named unless they beat your successes with Willpower when they accept.

Mana Cost: 7 Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Outside combat only Range: A group, guild, or city of willing signers Dice Pool: Intelligence + Circle Magic + Contract Magic Defense: None Effect: Over a full session of writing, bind up to your Heritage dots x100 willing signers. Penalties may be set up to Aggravated damage.

Mana Cost: 7, spent when written Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Written outside combat; the finished contract can be used any time Range: Signers Dice Pool: Intelligence + Circle Magic + Contract Magic Defense: None Effect: A contract that trades dots of an Attribute, Ability, or Merit between willing signers, up to half your Heritage dots, rounded up. The Storyteller may require a Sanity cost for large trades.

From "Peoples of the Known World" by Liris Kant, Third Chair of Natural Philosophy, Monsera University I have never met a pure blooded Dragonfolk. I have met several of mixed heritage, corresponded with two more, and read everything the Monsera University library holds on the subject, which is not much. The pure blooded do not oppose scholarship. They decline to be its subject. What is broadly understood about the pure blooded is this: they are genderless, hatched from eggs, androgynous in appearance, and fixed in number. How the population stays fixed is a private matter involving soul reincarnation, and they do not discuss it. Asking will not get an answer. Dragonfolk society is hierarchical, with the pure blooded at the top. Below that, rank depends on ability, not lineage. A first generation descendant and a twelfth generation descendant are treated as equals. What matters is demonstrated, ongoing capability. As a result, Dragonfolk are direct in their judgments and expect directness in return. Mixed heritage Dragonfolk are the ones the wider world meets, and they are rare. Scale patterns show on their skin in certain light, and their eye colors are uncommon in other heritages. People around them describe a sense of weight in the air. I dismissed this as romantic exaggeration until I met my third Dragonfolk. Older texts call them cold and contemptuous of lesser heritages. The Dragonfolk I interviewed found this either offensive or funny. In my experience they are direct and patient, and when something interests them, they give it complete attention. Mixed heritage Dragonfolk live about a thousand years. They are rarely in a hurry and find the urgency of shorter lived peoples somewhat comic. They are mostly polite about it.

Average Lifespan: 1000 years. Innate Attribute (choose 1, note Innate on sheet): Strength: For a character whose raw physical power and draconic might define them. Fortitude: For a character whose natural toughness and resilience define them. Innate Flaw - Intimidating: Dragonfolk are rare in the world and rumors about their nature have spread far and wide. Dragonfolk suffer a 1 die penalty on Expression rolls as others struggle to read them or feel at ease around them. Attribute Flaw - Social: Social attributes cannot be your Affinity column. They can only be your Standard or Aversion column. Heritage Merit (choose 1, record in Merits, Flaws, and Backgrounds section): Greater Mana Usage: Each dot in this merit adds 1 to the character's maximum Mana Per Turn beyond the standard calculation. Dragon's Might: Grants a free specialty in Melee or Martial Arts called Dragon's Might, providing a bonus die on attack rolls that leverage raw physical strength.

Mixed heritage Dragonfolk carry a weight that other people can feel in the air. Dragon Blood is that inheritance made active: scales, breath, wings, and a presence that presses down on everyone nearby. Dragon breath is raw draconic force and has no element. Primary: Strength + Martial Arts or Melee + Dragon Blood Secondary: Fortitude + Presence + Dragon Blood Extra mana: Attack or damage. 1 die per mana, up to your Dragon Blood dots or Max Mana Per Turn, whichever comes first.

Mana Cost: 1, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Defense, Attuned Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, gain Armor equal to half your Heritage dots, rounded up.

Mana Cost: 1, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Enhancement, Attuned Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, add your Heritage dots to Presence rolls made to intimidate or command attention.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Instant Type: Attack Use: Combat Range: One target in an adjacent zone Dice Pool: Strength + Martial Arts or Melee + Dragon Blood Defense: Target's choice of defense Effect: Breathe raw draconic force at the target.

Mana Cost: 2, upkeep 1 each Upkeep Phase Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Debuff, Persistent Use: Combat Range: All adjacent zones Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While maintained, enemies in range suffer -1 die on Dodge rolls.

Mana Cost: 3, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Enhancement, Attuned Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, your natural weapons have a rating equal to your Heritage dots, and attacks with them ignore Armor equal to half your Heritage dots, rounded up.

Mana Cost: 3 Speed: Reaction Type: Defense Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: Fortitude + Presence + Dragon Blood Defense: None Effect: When resisting fear or mental control, roll this dice pool instead of your normal roll.

Mana Cost: 4 Speed: Instant Type: Attack Use: Combat Range: Cone: all zones directly and diagonally forward of you Dice Pool: Strength + Martial Arts or Melee + Dragon Blood Defense: Target's choice of defense Effect: Dragon Breath against every target in the cone. Roll once; each target defends separately.

Mana Cost: 4, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Movement, Attuned Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, you manifest wings and fly at double your normal movement.

Mana Cost: 5, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Defense, Attuned Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, add your Heritage dots to your BDT. You are immune to the Burning and Chilled conditions.

Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Instant Type: Debuff Use: Combat Range: All enemies in sight Dice Pool: Fortitude + Presence + Dragon Blood Defense: Composure + Presence Effect: Each enemy resists with Composure + Presence. Each one you beat suffers -2 dice to attack you for the rest of the scene.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Instant Type: Attack Use: Combat Range: Straight line across the battlefield Dice Pool: Strength + Martial Arts or Melee + Dragon Blood Defense: Target's choice of defense Effect: Dragon Breath in a straight line. Each target defends separately. Damage does not fall off with distance.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Instant Type: Debuff Use: Combat Range: Up to 3 connected zones in sight Dice Pool: Fortitude + Presence + Dragon Blood Defense: Strength + Athletics Effect: Each enemy in range resists with Strength + Athletics. Each one you beat is knocked prone and cannot stand on their next turn.

Mana Cost: 7, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Enhancement, Attuned Use: Combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: Target's choice of defense against Breath Cone Effect: While attuned, you take a partial dragon form: you fly, your BDT doubles, and once per turn you may cast Breath Cone without its AP cost. You still pay its mana.

Dryads, Satyrs, Myconids, and similar. Fey monsters exist slightly sideways from the rest of the world. From Liris Kant's entry on the monster peoples The Fey, dryads, satyrs, myconids, and their relations, follow an internal logic that is consistent but does not match that of other peoples. Time works differently for them. Commerce is not something they are ignorant of. They simply do not grasp it. In Monsera they live where ambient mana is thickest, and the city has built around their trees rather than through them.

Average Lifespan: 400 years, though some Fey are Immortal (Storyteller decides). Innate Attribute (choose 1, note Innate on sheet): Charisma: For a character whose otherworldly presence and natural magnetism define them. Wisdom: For a character whose deep attunement to natural and magical forces define them. Innate Flaw - Otherworldly: Fey monsters suffer a penalty die on Commerce rolls. The mortal preoccupation with money and transactions is something they understand intellectually but struggle to engage with naturally. Attribute Flaw - Physical: Physical attributes cannot be your Affinity column. They can only be your Standard or Aversion column. Heritage Merit (choose 1, record in Merits, Flaws, and Backgrounds section): Nature Bond: Grants a free specialty in Survival reflecting their deep and instinctive connection to natural environments and living things. Wellspring: A dotted merit. During combat, you may gain 1 additional mana during your Upkeep Phase. You can do this a number of times per combat equal to your dots in this merit.

Fey Magic works the way a cartoon character pulls a mallet out of nowhere: the Fey imagines a thing hard enough and it is simply there. It is rarely deadly, because most Fey do not enjoy imagining harm. Good hearted Fey tend to be wonderful healers, since nothing is easier for them than picturing a friend feeling better. Primary: Wisdom + Expression + Fey Magic Secondary: Charisma + Attunement + Fey Magic Extra mana: Attack or damage. 1 die per mana, up to your Fey Magic dots or Max Mana Per Turn, whichever comes first. Fey from the Dreeming, where kind and wondrous beliefs take shape, tend to use their magic for protection, healing, and fun. Fey from the Seeming, where fears and dark tales are made real, tend to aim theirs at harm, fear, and discomfort. Healing spells use the healing tiers described in the Healing section at the start of this chapter.

Mana Cost: 1, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Attuned Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, a small ordinary object you imagine stays in your hand: a cup, a rope, a frying pan. It vanishes when the attunement ends.

Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Reaction Type: Defense Use: Combat Range: One ally in sight Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: Once per scene, an ally who would be hit is somehow in an adjacent zone instead. The attack misses.
Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Instant Type: Healing Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self or one ally in sight Dice Pool: Wisdom + Expression + Fey Magic Defense: None Effect: Expert healing.

During each Upkeep Phase it may move one zone, or attack one enemy in a zone adjacent to it using your dice pool.

It cannot be a creature, a magic item, or anything that acts on its own. Everything you made vanishes when the spell ends.

From "Peoples of the Known World" by Liris Kant, Third Chair of Natural Philosophy, Monsera University The Fishfolk are among the most important peoples in Terrana, and most of Terrana does not know it. For most of recorded history they have done work of great consequence without recognition, and they appear content with that. They favor the cold, deep northern and southern reaches of the Ringus Sea. Many visit or live in Monsera. They speak and listen like anyone else, but their faces do not show subtle emotional shifts. Mild amusement and mild irritation can look identical. Strong emotions such as delight or grief are obvious. The middle range takes patience to read. On average they are more naturally gifted with magic than the Merfolk, a point the two heritages still debate. The clearest example is the Tidewardens, the Fishfolk mages who maintain the seal over the Void Opening at the bottom of the Ringus Sea. They are not priests, politicians, or a formal institution. They are sea mages who inherited the duty and carry it steadily. Until recently, most of the world did not know the seal existed. People knew only that something enormous periodically rose from the Ringus Sea and attacked whatever was nearest, usually Monster Island before it became Monsera. Few connected those attacks to the Void Opening or to the Fishfolk holding it shut. The seal slows the Opening's growth and reduces how often and how badly things emerge. It is a pressure valve, not a cure. When pressure exceeds the seal, a breach occurs. The Fishfolk deal with the smaller Voidlings themselves. The Kaiju require the Hero Rangers Corps. This division of labor existed informally before the Corps was founded. Fishfolk live about two hundred years and tend to spend that time on understanding rather than accumulation. The Tidewardens regard the Void neither with fear nor with dismissal, but with the careful attention of people who have studied a dangerous thing for a long time. They intermarry with the Merfolk fairly often. The two heritages are clear about their differences and have never let those differences become distance.

Average Lifespan: 200 years. Innate Attribute (choose 1, note Innate on sheet): Fortitude: For a character whose physical resilience and deep water endurance define them. Intelligence: For a character whose sharp analytical mind and heightened cognitive capacity define them. Innate Flaw - Fisheye: Fishfolk facial features make visual expression extremely difficult for others to read. Fishfolk suffer a 1 die penalty on all Expression rolls. Attribute Flaw - Social: Social attributes cannot be your Affinity column. They can only be your Standard or Aversion column. Heritage Merit (choose 1, record in Merits, Flaws, and Backgrounds section): Water Sense: Grants a free specialty in Magic called Water Sense, providing a bonus die on Water Magic rolls reflecting the Fishfolk's natural attunement to aquatic mana. Deep Dweller: Grants a free specialty in Endurance called Deep Dweller, providing a bonus die on Endurance rolls involving pressure, depth, sustained physical stress, and harsh environmental conditions.

The magic of the Tidewardens is the magic every Fishfolk carries in some measure: pressure, depth, and the patient work of keeping things from the Void where they belong. It senses, binds, seals, and when it must, crushes. Primary: Intelligence + Attunement + Tidewarden Secondary: Fortitude + Endurance + Tidewarden Extra mana: Attack or damage. 1 die per mana, up to your Tidewarden dots or Max Mana Per Turn, whichever comes first.

Mana Cost: 1, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Attuned Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, add your Heritage dots to rolls to detect Void-touched creatures and Void energy within a number of zones equal to your Tidewarden dots.

Mana Cost: 1 Speed: Reaction Type: Defense Use: Combat and outside combat Range: Self Dice Pool: Fortitude + Endurance + Tidewarden Defense: None Effect: When resisting crushing force, depth, or pressure, roll this dice pool instead of your normal roll.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Instant Type: Debuff Use: Combat Range: One target in an adjacent zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Attunement + Tidewarden Defense: Fortitude + Endurance Effect: The target resists with Fortitude + Endurance. If you beat them, they suffer -2 dice on physical rolls on their next turn.

Mana Cost: 2, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Attuned Use: Combat and outside combat Range: One creature in sight Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, you know where the marked creature is.

Mana Cost: 3, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Defense, Attuned Use: Combat Range: Self or one ally in an adjacent zone Dice Pool: None Defense: None Effect: While attuned, the target adds your Heritage dots to their BDT against Voidlings and Void entities.

Mana Cost: 3 Speed: Instant Type: Debuff Use: Combat Range: One target in sight Dice Pool: Intelligence + Attunement + Tidewarden Defense: Strength + Athletics Effect: The target resists with Strength + Athletics. If you beat them, they are pulled one zone toward you.

Mana Cost: 4 Speed: Instant Type: Debuff Use: Combat Range: One Voidling or conjuration in sight Dice Pool: Intelligence + Attunement + Tidewarden Defense: Willpower, or a conjuration's maker's dice pool Effect: The target resists with Willpower, or a conjuration with its maker's dice pool. If you beat it, it cannot act until the end of its next turn.

Mana Cost: 4 Speed: Instant Type: Attack Use: Combat Range: One target in sight Dice Pool: Intelligence + Attunement + Tidewarden Defense: Fortitude + Endurance Effect: Water pressure strikes the target. They defend with Fortitude + Endurance instead of Dodge, and Armor does not apply.

Mana Cost: 5, upkeep 4 each Upkeep Phase Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Persistent Use: Combat and outside combat Range: One zone in sight Dice Pool: Intelligence + Attunement + Tidewarden Defense: Strength + Athletics Effect: Roll when cast. While maintained, nothing can enter or leave the zone without beating your successes with Strength + Athletics.

Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Reaction Type: Defense Use: Combat Range: Self or one ally in sight Dice Pool: Fortitude + Endurance + Tidewarden Defense: None Effect: When the target is attacked, roll your dice pool. Each success reduces the attacker's successes by 1.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Instant Type: Utility Use: Combat Range: One conjuration, Voidling, or Void entity in sight Dice Pool: Intelligence + Attunement + Tidewarden Defense: Willpower, or a conjuration's maker's dice pool Effect: The target resists with Willpower, or a conjuration with its maker's dice pool. If you beat it and its rank is no higher than your Heritage dots, it is driven out of the world. A banished conjuration ends.

Mana Cost: 6, upkeep 5 each Upkeep Phase Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Debuff, Persistent Use: Combat Range: Up to 3 connected zones in sight Dice Pool: Intelligence + Attunement + Tidewarden Defense: None Effect: While maintained, enemies in those zones suffer -2 dice, and moving through them costs double AP.

Mana Cost: 7 Speed: Downtime Type: Utility Use: Outside combat only Range: One Void rift, portal, or opening Dice Pool: Intelligence + Attunement + Tidewarden Defense: None Effect: Over a full scene of ritual work, close the opening. The great Void Opening of the Ringus Sea can only be slowed, never sealed, by one warden alone.

Mana Cost: 7, upkeep 6 each Upkeep Phase Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Debuff, Persistent Use: Combat Range: All Void entities in sight Dice Pool: Intelligence + Attunement + Tidewarden Defense: None Effect: While maintained, each Void entity in sight gains the Rooted condition and takes damage equal to your Heritage dots during each Upkeep Phase.

Ghosts and spirits: souls that stayed in the world after their bodies were lost. Sustained by mana, bound to an anchor, and able to touch the world only through Manifestation. Not available at character creation. From Liris Kant's entry on the monster peoples Incorporeal Undead are what remains when a soul stays after its body is gone. Like the Corporeal Undead they are sustained by mana, but they have no body to hold it. Every one I have met was tied to something: a house, a ring, a grandchild. They call it their anchor. Away from it they thin out. I watched one follow a friend two streets from her own doorstep, then turn back, barely visible. Nobody is born a ghost. Each of them died first. Some will tell you how it happened and some will not. Speaking with them takes patience. The newly dead can barely make themselves heard. The older ones can move objects, borrow bodies, and in a few cases build something close to a body of their own. Those are rare, and they do not like being studied.

Average Lifespan: Immortal, as long as their mana and anchor last. Innate Attribute: Keeps the Innate Attribute of the heritage the character had in life. Innate Flaw - Insubstantial: Incorporeal Undead cannot touch, hold, or carry anything physical, and nothing physical can touch them, except through Manifestation spells. They pass through ordinary walls, doors, and objects. They are bound to an anchor (see Anchor). Attribute Flaw: Keep the Attribute Flaw of your former heritage. Becoming Incorporeal: Incorporeal Undead cannot be chosen at character creation. A character can only become one during play, with Storyteller approval, in one of three ways. Unfinished Business: The character dies without choosing to die, and their body is cremated or destroyed before they can be resurrected. If something holds them that they could not let go of, the soul stays behind. Soul Binding: A high rank Shade Magic user, such as a necromancer or lich, tears the soul from a dying or dead body and binds it to an anchor. The ghost begins under that caster's control, like imprinted undead. Failed Resurrection: A resurrection fails after the soul has partly returned. It can no longer enter the body, and it does not leave. What Carries Over: The character keeps their Attributes, Abilities, Merits, Magical Knowledges, and the Innate Attribute of their former heritage. They gain 1 free dot in Manifestation and choose a Heritage Merit below. Their former Heritage magic and any Combat Styles that need a body go dormant. They can be used only while Full Manifestation, Reclaim Flesh, or a possession is active. Casting schools still work, since a spell is shaped mana and so is a ghost. Anchor: Every Incorporeal Undead is bound to an anchor: a place, an object, or a person. For each scene spent outside the immediate vicinity of the anchor, such as the house it sits in or the room its person is in, the character's maximum mana pool drops by 1. The lost maximum returns after a full scene spent back at the anchor. If the maximum reaches 0, the character fades and cannot act until they return to the anchor. If the anchor is destroyed, they have one session to bind themselves to a new anchor of similar importance, or they fade permanently. Damage: Ordinary physical attacks pass through Incorporeal Undead. Magic, Battle Aura, and enchanted weapons hit them normally. A Bright Magic hit is treated as meeting the next-higher damage threshold. While Full Manifestation or Reclaim Flesh is active, physical attacks harm them as well. Heritage Merit (choose 1, record in Merits, Flaws, and Backgrounds section): Unseen: Grants a free specialty in Stealth called Unseen, providing a bonus die to rolls to stay unnoticed. Grave Voice: Grants a free specialty in Insight called Grave Voice, providing a bonus die to read the intentions of the living and the dead.

A ghost begins with almost no hold on the world. Manifestation is how that hold grows: first being felt, then seen, then touching things, then borrowing bodies, and at its height building a body of its own for a while. Primary: Composure + Attunement + Manifestation Secondary: Charisma + Presence + Manifestation Extra mana: Attack or damage. 1 die per mana, up to your Manifestation dots or Max Mana Per Turn, whichever comes first.

Mana Cost: 1, attuned (stays committed) Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Attuned Use: Combat and outside combat Range: All adjacent zones Dice Pool: Composure + Attunement + Manifestation Defense: None Effect: While attuned, the air in all adjacent zones turns cold and lights there flicker. Living creatures in range feel that something is present.

Mana Cost: 1 Speed: Instant Type: Utility Use: Combat and outside combat Range: One living creature in sight Dice Pool: Charisma + Presence + Manifestation Defense: None Effect: The target hears up to one sentence from you. No one else hears it.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Instant Type: Utility Use: Combat and outside combat Range: One small object in an adjacent zone Dice Pool: Composure + Attunement + Manifestation Defense: None Effect: Move one object weighing a few pounds or less up to one zone, such as opening an unlocked door, tipping a cup, or sliding a key. An object someone is holding cannot be moved.

From "Peoples of the Known World" by Liris Kant, Third Chair of Natural Philosophy, Monsera University Merfolk and Fishfolk are often confused in popular literature, and both find this irritating. Both are aquatic heritages. Beyond that they differ considerably. Merfolk favor the warmer eastern and western reaches of the Ringus Sea. They live in coastal settlements there, in Monsera's water districts, and elsewhere as curiosity takes them. They shift between tail and legs at will, smoothly and easily. Their appearance spans aquatic life broadly. Some have dolphin coloring, some shark markings, some tentacles in place of fins. Most share a strong presence, though it takes different forms. Some have voices that quiet a room. Others have a striking appearance that people notice before anything else. They intermarry with Fishfolk fairly often. The distinction between the two heritages has never meant hostility. Children of these marriages carry both lines. The shift between legs and tail is triggered involuntarily by a heavy, unexpected splash of water. It is not painful, but Merfolk describe it as a reflex and an indignity. They cannot will their legs back. They must dry off or wait, preferably in private. Splashing a Merfolk is a social error that often ends a friendship before it starts.

Failure means they are grounded until they dry off or choose to reenter water fully. Attribute Flaw - Mental: Mental attributes cannot be your Affinity column. They can only be your Standard or Aversion column. Striking Beauty: Grants a free specialty in either Expression or Performance (player's choice), reflecting the Merfolk's natural magnetism and captivating presence.

From "Peoples of the Known World" by Liris Kant, Third Chair of Natural Philosophy, Monsera University I met Roxy Migurdia once, as a student at Monsera University, where she was a guest of the faculty. She was small and blue haired and said little until the formal lecture ended. She is the reason most of the world knows the Migurd exist, and she belongs in any honest account of her people. The Migurd live in the desert of the Demon Continent, in homes built into the shells of giant stone turtles. Over generations the shells have become architecture. They are about half a foot shorter than Dwarves and taller than Halflings. Every Migurd has blue hair, from pale ice blue to deep navy, and the exact shade helps tell individuals apart. They stop aging in appearance in their twenties and resume around their hundred and fiftieth year, living about two hundred years in total. A Migurd who looks twenty five may be a century and a half old. Migurd speak to one another by telepathy, with no mana and no effort. Much of what other peoples handle through formal governance, such as settling disputes, sharing information, and building consensus, happens directly and with little room for misunderstanding. They still have a chief and a tribal structure. Reaching other heritages telepathically costs mana and effort and is less precise. As a result, many Migurd find spoken language awkward. Words lose and distort meaning in ways telepathy does not. Verbal persuasion in particular feels unnatural to them. Roxy was born without telepathy. Her community was not unkind, but it did not know what to do with her, and she left. When I met her, she carried that history lightly. That same evening she introduced me to Sylphiette, her former student and one of the finest mages of her generation. The Migurd once lived near the Superd on the Demon Continent and were among the first to suffer the aftermath of the Laplace War. That fear lasted a long time. With the Superd now in Biheiril and the truth of the war better understood, it has faded. The Migurd I spoke with treat it as history.

From "Peoples of the Known World" by Liris Kant, Third Chair of Natural Philosophy, Monsera University The Skyfolk live on the Heaven Continent, three thousand meters above sea level. Geography and custom have kept them largely separate from the rest of Terrana for all of recorded history. I have met four. All Skyfolk have wings, but their appearance otherwise varies as widely as Hyumans and birds combined. Skyfolk from different regions of the Heaven Continent can look nothing alike. They live about four hundred years. Skyfolk do not experience humor. This is not reserve or custom. It is a difference in how they process social information, and they treat it as a fact about themselves, the way someone might treat being unable to see certain colors. Two of the four I met had tried to study humor methodically. Neither succeeded, and both found the attempt interesting. They are rare enough in the lower world that one walking through Monsera or Breakwater stops traffic. They are aware of this and indifferent to it. They are detached, though not cold, and they tend to view events against a very long timeline. Courtship resembles that of birds. A male must build a nest or dwelling suitable for raising young before he is considered as a partner, and his plumage weighs heavily in how he is received. Once a year the Heaven Continent holds sky dancing, a competitive aerial display performed at high altitude and judged by females. I have not been invited, and I have decided it would be impolite to ask. Skyfolk mate for life, and with a four hundred year lifespan a partnership can last three centuries. After a partner dies, most never seek another. The Skyfolk I asked said another partnership would not be impossible, only beside the point. A small number of immortal Skyfolk exist, described across many cultures as angelic in appearance. I have not met one. Skyfolk asked about them give answers that are technically responsive and contain no information.

Skyfolk suffer a 1 die penalty on Insight rolls when dealing with non-Skyfolk heritages. Attribute Flaw - Social: Social attributes cannot be your Affinity column. They can only be your Standard or Aversion column. Flight: Skyfolk fly naturally at double their normal movement without magic. Wind Born: Grants a free specialty in Endurance called Wind Born, providing a bonus die on Endurance rolls made while airborne or against environmental hazards related to altitude, wind, and weather.

Slimes. Living mana with a soul. Immortal. From Liris Kant's entry on the monster peoples Most slimes are not people. The ones that fill sewers and dungeon floors are mana with a body and nothing behind it. A few are different. They think, speak, and remember, and they are among the rarest peoples in Terrana. By the university’s best count there are fewer than a thousand sentient slimes alive today. Monsera University has studied them for most of a century, with the help of slimes who volunteered. Our conclusion, still debated, is that a sentient slime is a soul made physical by mana. Every slime may carry the start of one, but most never wake. The comparison my colleagues use is reproductive: a father produces countless sperm, and almost none become a person. Awakening is rare in the same way. A newly awakened slime is a round, glossy blob. With time it learns to hold other shapes, first rounded and shining, later close enough to fool anyone. Slimes have no typical gender. They take one if they like, or none. Slimes have produced some of Monsera’s most notable philosophers, perhaps because a being with no fixed shape has had to think carefully about what stays the same.

Average Lifespan: Immortal (Mana Bound). Mana Bound: A slime that dies without choosing to is not gone while its body still holds mana. Its mana counts down as normal ( Chapter 11 ), but it does not need Resurrection. Healing works on it the same as on a living character, and it heals naturally as if resting. When all of its damage is removed, it wakes with whatever mana it has left. If its mana reaches 0 first, it dies for good. A slime that chose Blaze of Glory dies like anyone else. Innate Attribute (choose 1, note Innate on sheet): Fortitude: For a character whose soft, shock-absorbing body defines them. Wisdom: For a character whose patient, reflective mind defines them. Innate Flaw - Bound to Mana: When your Mana Pool is empty, you lose any form from Take Shape and return to your blob form until you recover at least 1 mana. In blob form you suffer a 1 die penalty on rolls that need hands. Attribute Flaw - Social: Social attributes cannot be your Affinity column. They can only be your Standard or Aversion column. Heritage Merit (choose 1, record in Merits, Flaws, and Backgrounds section): Elastic: Grants a free specialty in Acrobatics called Elastic, providing a bonus die on rolls to squeeze through gaps, stretch, or land a fall. Hidden Pocket: You can store one hand-sized object inside your body. A normal search cannot find it, and drawing it costs no AP.

A slime’s body is mana that has learned to hold a shape. Morph is the control of that body, from a simple disguise to extra limbs, wings, and a hide like stone. Every rank of Morph grants a Default Ability, as well as the choice of an A or B spell. Primary: Dexterity + Martial Arts + Morph Secondary: Fortitude + Endurance + Morph Extra mana: Attack or damage. 1 die per mana, up to your Morph dots or Max Mana Per Turn, whichever comes first.

Default Ability Take Shape Both You can hold a humanoid or animal form about your own size instead of your blob form. Changing form costs 1 AP in combat. The form is smooth, rounded, and glossy, and anyone can tell you are a slime. Your stats do not change with your form.
