The affected zones become difficult terrain for the remainder of the scene (movement costs 1 additional AP). Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. The caster's zone is unaffected. The ground around the caster becomes unreliable all at once. Earth at this rank can sink an entire zone into rubble or call a barrage of stone down from above. Default Ability: Unyielding Ground (Permanent) Difficult terrain created by your Earth spells costs enemies 1 additional AP to move through, and you and your allies ignore it.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, AoE, CC, Earth Range: AoE-4 (2x2 zone area), any targeted zone within line of sight Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Earth dots Effect: A chunk of dense earth the size of a room falls from above onto a 2x2 zone area. Caster rolls once. Every target in the area must defend separately. All targets hit are Knocked Down. Any target hit by 4 or more excess successes is also pinned under debris (Rooted until they succeed on Strength + Athletics vs cast successes as an action). The affected zones become difficult terrain. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. A great deal of earth falls on a great deal of people at once.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Conjuration, Persistent, Earth Range: Caster's zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Earth dots Effect: Stone walls, roof, and floor rise around the caster's zone, forming a sealed fortification. The structure blocks movement across all four borders unless a gate is designated at cast time. The structure has a Vitality pool equal to triple the cast successes (split evenly across the four walls). Each wall section must be destroyed separately. Attacks targeting the interior must breach a wall first. Upkeep: 5. A stone fort rises from the ground in a turn. The caster is inside it. Earth at this rank can move the ground itself or turn the caster into something that barely qualifies as a creature anymore. Default Ability: Mountain's Weight (Permanent) A target Knocked Down by your Earth spells is also Rooted until their next Upkeep Phase.

Mana Cost: 7 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, AoE, CC, Earth Range: All zones within line of sight Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Earth dots Effect: The caster moves the ground. Every zone within line of sight shifts by 1 zone in a direction the caster chooses (or different directions per zone at the cost of 1 additional mana per zone with varying directions). Any target in a zone that shifts must roll Dexterity + Acrobatics vs cast successes or be Knocked Down and take damage equal to excess successes. Zones that shift into other zones cause both to become difficult terrain. The caster's zone does not shift. The caster moves the world. Only a little. It is enough.

Mana Cost: 7 Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Enhancement, Persistent, Earth Range: Self Dice Pool: Fortitude + Magic + Earth dots Effect: The caster's body is encased and augmented by a massive form of living stone, doubling their size and dramatically altering their capabilities. Strength and Fortitude each gain dots equal to cast successes (up to Earth dots maximum). All melee attacks deal additional damage equal to Earth dots. The caster gains immunity to Knocked Down and Rooted conditions. The caster's movement is reduced by 2 zones while active. Upkeep: 6. The caster stops being a person and starts being a problem.

Nature Magic is the school of living growth, vines, spores, and organic force. Its spells can root and entangle targets, create terrain effects, and deal damage over time. Nature can assign mana to either the attack roll or the damage roll. It carries elemental advantages against Earth and Air and is weakest against Fire and Water. Elemental interactions: +2 against Earth, +1 against Air, -1 against Water, -2 against Fire. Nature at this rank grows vines and throws thorns. The caster can work with the living world in direct and basic ways. Default Ability: Forest Sense (Permanent) You gain 1 bonus die on Survival rolls in natural wilderness, and you can always identify a plant and what it does.

Mana Cost: 1 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, Nature Range: Adjacent zone Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Nature dots Effect: A sharp organic projectile launches at a target in an adjacent zone. On a hit deals damage equal to excess successes. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. A thorn. Much faster than normal thorns.

Mana Cost: 1 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Nature Range: Adjacent zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Nature dots Effect: Vines erupt from the ground, seize a target in an adjacent zone, and drag them. On a success the target is pulled 1 zone toward the caster. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. Outside of combat, Entangle can bind an unresisting object or tie down cargo, and the vines stay until cut. Vines grab a target and hold on. Nature can now be used across greater distances and begins to poison. Default Ability: Bloom (1 mana, Instant) Make a plant grow a full season in moments: ripen fruit, sprout a seed into a sapling, or spread a vine across a wall.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, CC, Nature Range: Targeted Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Nature dots Effect: A vine lashes out at a target within line of sight. On a hit deals damage equal to excess successes. Any target hit must roll Strength + Athletics vs cast successes or be pulled 1 zone toward the caster. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. A vine that reaches and pulls.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, Nature Range: Adjacent zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Nature dots Effect: A cloud of toxic spores bursts at a target in an adjacent zone. Target must roll Fortitude + Endurance vs cast successes. Failure applies the Poisoned condition with a damage value of 1 per 2 excess successes (minimum 1). The Poisoned condition deals its damage value at each Upkeep Phase until the condition ends or the target is treated. Fire Magic ignites the spores and ends the condition but deals 1 damage. Defend: Fortitude + Endurance. A burst of organic poison. Invisible. Persistent. The caster can fill zones with growth and begin to use nature as a barrier. Default Ability: Thornhide (Attuned: holds 2 of your M/T while active) Thorns grow along your skin and clothing. Any target that hits you with a melee attack takes 1 damage.

Mana Cost: 3 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, AoE, Nature Range: AoE-Cone Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Nature dots Effect: A spray of razor-sharp thorns erupts in a cone from the caster, covering all zones directly in front and diagonally forward. Caster rolls once. Each target defends separately. All targets hit gain the Bleeding condition. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. A wide spray of thorns. Messy. Effective.

Mana Cost: 3 Speed: Instant Type: Conjuration, Persistent, Nature Range: Adjacent zone border Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Nature dots Effect: A dense curtain of vines rises along a zone border. The vines block passage: any target attempting to cross must roll Strength + Athletics vs cast successes or become Rooted for 1 turn. On success, they cross but their movement for this turn ends. The curtain has a Vitality pool equal to double the cast successes. Fire Magic reduces the Vitality pool by the Fire caster's successes. Upkeep: 2. A wall of vines that would rather hold than block. Nature can now seize targets from range and fill entire zones with suffocating growth. Default Ability: Deep Roots (Permanent) Targets Rooted by your Nature spells need 1 additional success to break free.

Mana Cost: 4 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, Persistent, CC, Nature Range: Targeted Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Nature dots Effect: Roots erupt and seize a target. On a hit the target gains the Rooted condition. Each Upkeep Phase the target remains Rooted, they also take damage equal to the original cast successes as the roots tighten. The target may attempt Strength + Athletics vs cast successes during their Upkeep Phase to break free. Fire Magic applied to the target ends the effect. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. Roots that seize and keep tightening.

Mana Cost: 4 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Persistent, CC, Nature Range: Zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Nature dots Effect: Dense plant growth erupts across the zone. Movement into or through the zone costs 2 additional AP. Targets entering the zone roll Dexterity + Dodge vs cast successes or become Rooted until their next Upkeep Phase. Fire Magic reduces cast successes by the Fire caster's successes. Upkeep: 3. The zone becomes a problem for anyone who needs to move through it. Nature can lash multiple targets at once and open the wild for allies to move through. Default Ability: Plant Memory (3 mana, Instant) Touch a plant and ask it what it witnessed in the last day. It answers with simple impressions of who passed and what happened.

Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, AoE, Nature Range: Zone Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Nature dots Effect: Thorns erupt from the ground throughout a zone, targeting all targets in it simultaneously. Caster rolls once and applies the same attack successes to all targets. Each defends separately. All targets hit gain the Bleeding condition. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. The caster may exclude zones from the effect if they wish, targeting fewer than the full zone. The entire zone becomes hostile ground.

Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Buff, Persistent, Nature Range: Self and allies in adjacent zones, up to Nature dots in targets Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Nature dots Effect: The wild opens for the caster and their allies. While active, affected targets ignore difficult terrain created by plants or natural ground, cannot be Rooted by Nature Magic or plant-based effects, and gain bonus dice equal to cast successes on Stealth rolls in zones with plant growth. Upkeep: 4. Branches part. Roots settle. The forest lets you through. Nature at this rank can seize multiple targets at once or create a permanent living forest on the battlefield. Default Ability: Virulence (Permanent) Poisoned conditions from your Nature spells start with a damage value 2 higher.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, AoE, Persistent, CC, Nature Range: AoE, up to Nature dots zones chosen by caster Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Nature dots Effect: The caster fills a number of zones up to their Nature dots with thorns and roots. In all chosen zones: any target entering or remaining must roll Dexterity + Dodge vs cast successes or become Rooted. Any target who is Rooted takes damage equal to cast successes each Upkeep Phase. Fire Magic in a targeted zone reduces cast successes in that zone. Upkeep: 5. A spreading thicket that grabs and holds everything it can reach.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Defense, Persistent, Nature Range: Self Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Nature dots Effect: Living bark and vine weave around the caster in a shifting organic shell. Add cast successes to the caster's BDT against physical attacks. When the caster takes damage while this is active, the armor regenerates 1 success to its BDT bonus at each Upkeep Phase (the natural regeneration maintains the shell). Fire attacks bypass the regeneration: each Fire attack reduces the DT bonus by the Fire caster's school dots. Upkeep: 5. The caster is wrapped in something alive. It grows back when damaged. Nature at this rank can overwhelm the battlefield with life or draw all the life out of an area. Default Ability: Verdant Path (Attuned: holds 4 of your M/T while active) Plants surge up wherever you walk. Each zone you leave becomes difficult terrain for enemies until the start of the next Upkeep Phase.

Mana Cost: 7 Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Conjuration, Persistent, CC, Nature Range: All zones within line of sight Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Nature dots Effect: A massive tree erupts from the ground and sends roots and branches throughout the entire visible area. Every visible zone gains the effects of Overgrowth Zone using the cast successes as the roll result. Any target in a zone when the tree erupts must roll Dexterity + Dodge vs cast successes or be immediately Rooted. The tree itself occupies the caster's zone and has a Vitality pool equal to triple the cast successes. If the tree's pool reaches 0, all Overgrowth effects end simultaneously. Upkeep: 6. A tree grows. Immediately and everywhere. The battlefield adapts to the tree.

Mana Cost: 7 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, AoE, Persistent, Nature Range: All zones within line of sight Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Nature dots Effect: The caster drains all living energy from the visible area. Caster rolls once. Every living target in every visible zone must resist. Each target resists separately. On a failure targets take damage equal to excess successes and gain the Poisoned condition with a value equal to the original cast successes. All natural plant material in the affected zones withers and dies, destroying any existing Nature Magic terrain effects in those zones. Undead targets in the zones are unaffected. Defend: Fortitude + Endurance. Everything green dies. The people in it follow.

Bright Magic is the school of radiant energy and illumination. It does not heal on its own; healing comes from combining Bright with other schools. It is the only school capable of transferring mana between characters. Bright damages undead, buffs living targets, and cannot harm the living through a standard Bright attack. Exceptions require specific high-rank spells that name the exception explicitly. Bright assigns mana to the attack roll only. Bright Magic has no elemental interactions with the five elemental schools. Its interactions are tied to living and undead targets. Bright at this rank produces light. The caster can direct radiant energy with purpose and find that it damages undead while leaving the living untouched. Default Ability: Sense Undead (Permanent) You always know when undead are in adjacent zones, even when they are hidden.

Mana Cost: 1 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, Bright, Undead Range: Adjacent zone Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Bright dots Effect: A bolt of radiant energy strikes a target in an adjacent zone. This attack only damages undead targets. Against a living target it deals no damage. On a hit against an undead target deals damage equal to excess successes. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. A flash of radiant energy. For most people, harmless. For undead, not.

Mana Cost: 1 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Bright Range: Zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Bright dots Effect: A flash of radiant light fills a zone. Every unlit non-magical light source in the zone (torches, lamps, candles) lights up and stays lit as ordinary flame. Any Dimmed effect in the zone ends if the Glow successes meet or exceed its cast successes. The shadows have nowhere left to sit. Bright can now reach further and begin to provide persistent support. Default Ability: Halo (Attuned: holds 1 of your M/T while active) A soft light surrounds you. Non-magical darkness has no effect on you, and you can light your surroundings at will.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, Bright, Undead Range: Targeted Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Bright dots Effect: A concentrated ray of radiant energy strikes an undead target at range. Only damages undead. On a hit deals damage equal to excess successes. Additionally, any active Shade Magic effects on the target lose 1 success from their pool on a successful hit. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. Radiant energy with reach. It strips shadow from what it touches.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Buff, Persistent, Bright Range: Touch or adjacent zone target Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Bright dots Effect: The caster charges a target with radiant energy, providing a minor but persistent benefit. Add cast successes as bonus dice to one specified roll type (attack, defense, or a single Attribute + Ability combination declared at cast time). This bonus applies until the effect ends. Upkeep: 1. A sustained radiant enhancement that makes one kind of task easier. The caster can flood a zone with radiant light that strengthens the living and weakens the undead. Default Ability: Radiance (Permanent) Your Bright attacks against undead ignore 1 point of the armor portion of their DT.

Mana Cost: 3 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, AoE, Bright, Undead Range: AoE-Cone Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Bright dots Effect: A cone of radiant energy erupts from the caster covering all zones directly in front and diagonally forward. Only damages undead targets. Living targets in the cone are unaffected. Caster rolls once. Each undead target in the cone defends separately. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. A burst of holy light that sweeps a cone of undead targets.

Mana Cost: 3 Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Buff, Persistent, Bright Range: Zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Bright dots Effect: Brilliant radiant light fills the zone. Living allies in the zone gain bonus dice equal to cast successes on all attack rolls. Undead enemies in the zone must roll Fortitude + Endurance vs cast successes at their Upkeep Phase or lose 1 mana. No one in the zone can benefit from darkness or Stealth while the Beacon holds. Shade Magic that meets or exceeds the cast successes dispels it. Upkeep: 2. A light so bright it feels like courage. The caster can transfer mana to allies and sweep radiant energy across an entire zone. Default Ability: Inspire (2 mana, Instant) An ally in an adjacent zone gains 1 bonus die on their next roll this turn.

Mana Cost: 4 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, AoE, Bright, Undead Range: Zone Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Bright dots Effect: A wave of radiant energy sweeps through an entire zone. Only damages undead targets in the zone. Living targets are unaffected. Caster rolls once and applies the same attack successes to all undead targets. Each undead target defends separately. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. The zone flares with radiant energy. Everything undead in it learns.

Mana Cost: 4 (spent by the caster; the amount transferred is separate) Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Bright Range: Touch or adjacent zone target Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Bright dots Effect: The caster transfers mana from their pool to a willing target. On a success, the caster may transfer up to their Bright dots in mana from their own pool to the target's pool, without exceeding the target's Mana Pool cap. The 4 mana cost is spent on the casting itself and is not part of the transferred amount. Can target living targets only. The caster opens a channel and lets mana flow. The only Bright ability that can do this. Bright can now break the hold on undead and begin to affect them with powerful single-target annihilation. Default Ability: Purity (Permanent) You gain bonus dice equal to half your Bright dots (rounded up) on resistance rolls against Shade Magic.

Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, Bright, Undead Range: Targeted Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Bright dots Effect: A concentrated beam of radiant energy locks onto an undead target. Only damages undead. On a hit deals damage equal to excess successes doubled. Additionally, any Shade Magic persistent effects on the target end immediately. On 5+ excess successes, the target must also roll Fortitude + Endurance vs cast successes or be Stunned (loses their next action). Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. Radiant energy that hits an undead target with twice the force. Then strips their shadows.

Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, CC, Bright, Undead Range: Zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Bright dots Effect: A wave of radiant authority rolls through the zone. Every undead target in the zone must resist separately. Mindless undead that fail flee directly away from the caster for turns equal to excess successes. Undead that were animated or are commanded by another caster are released from that command for the rest of the scene. Sentient undead that fail lose their next action. Defend: Composure + Insight. The dead remember, for a moment, that they were meant to rest. Bright can consecrate zones and strike all undead targets in sight simultaneously. Default Ability: Aura of Dawn (Attuned: holds 3 of your M/T while active) Undead in zones adjacent to you lose 1 die on attack rolls.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Persistent, Bright Range: Zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Bright dots Effect: Radiant energy is pressed into a zone, consecrating it. All undead targets in the zone take damage equal to cast successes each Upkeep Phase. All living targets in the zone gain cast successes as bonus dice on resistance rolls. Shade Magic attacks aimed at targets in the zone lose 1 success before resolving. Cannot be dispelled by Shade Magic below the cast successes value. Upkeep: 5. The zone is consecrated. The undead feel it immediately.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, AoE, Bright, Undead Range: AoE, all zones within line of sight Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Bright dots Effect: Pillars of radiant light descend on every visible zone simultaneously. Only damages undead targets. Living targets are unaffected. Caster rolls once and applies the same attack successes to all undead in all visible zones. Each undead target defends separately. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. Light falls everywhere at once. Every undead target in sight is addressed. Bright at this rank can burn an undead out of existence or pour so much radiant energy into a space that undead cannot exist within it. Default Ability: Sanctified (Permanent) When your Bright Magic opposes or dispels Shade Magic, your successes count double.

Mana Cost: 7 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, Bright, Undead Range: Targeted Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Bright dots Effect: A column of pure radiant energy strikes a single undead target. Only damages undead. On a hit deals damage equal to excess successes tripled. Any undead Incapacitated by this spell is destroyed outright and cannot rise again. Every Shade Magic persistent effect in the target's zone ends. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. There is no getting back up from this.

Mana Cost: 7 Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Persistent, Bright Range: All zones within line of sight Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Bright dots Effect: Radiant energy saturates the entire visible area at a level that undead cannot endure. Any undead target in any visible zone takes damage equal to cast successes each Upkeep Phase. Any undead who enters a visible zone takes the same damage immediately. The caster and all living allies in the area gain cast successes as a bonus DT pool against all attacks. Shade Magic attacks in the area lose 2 successes before resolving. Upkeep: 6. Cannot be dispelled by Shade Magic below the cast successes. The entire visible world is consecrated simultaneously. Undead cannot stand in it.

Shade Magic is the school of darkness, mana drain, and corruption. It damages living targets, buffs undead, obscures vision, and drains mana directly from a target's pool. It cannot harm undead through a standard Shade attack. Exceptions require specific spells that name them. Shade assigns mana to the damage roll only. Mana Bleed: Many Shade spells leave living targets losing mana at every Upkeep Phase (see How Casting Works). Ethereal Shade, available at higher ranks, locks a target to their base Mana recovery rate with no damage bonus applied, regardless of how much damage they have taken. Shade Magic has no elemental interactions with the five elemental schools. Its interactions are tied to living and undead targets. Shade at this rank produces darkness and begins to drain. The caster can direct shadow energy against living targets. Undead targets are immune to standard Shade damage but benefit from its other effects. Default Ability: Darksight (Permanent) You see in non-magical darkness as if it were lit.

Mana Cost: 1 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, Shade, Living Range: Adjacent zone Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Shade dots Effect: A bolt of shadow energy strikes a living target in an adjacent zone. Only damages living targets. Against undead it deals no damage. On a hit deals damage equal to excess successes. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. Shadow with force behind it. The living feel it.

Mana Cost: 1 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Shade Range: Zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Shade dots Effect: A breath of shadow snuffs out every non-magical light source in a zone (torches, lamps, candles). They stay out until relit. Any light created by Bright Magic in the zone ends if the Dim successes meet or exceed its cast successes. The light goes. Not all at once. But enough. Shade reaches further and begins to pull mana from living targets. Default Ability: Hush (1 mana, Instant) Every sound you make is muffled until the start of the next Upkeep Phase. You gain 2 bonus dice on Stealth rolls during that time.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, Drain, Shade, Living Range: Targeted Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Shade dots Effect: A bolt of shadow energy strikes a living target at range. Only damages living targets. On a hit deals damage equal to excess successes. Additionally, the target loses 1 mana directly from their pool per success on this attack. The mana is drained and lost. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. Shadow that drains as well as damages.

Mana Cost: 2 Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Persistent, Shade Range: Self Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Shade dots Effect: The caster wraps themselves in shadow, becoming harder to perceive. While active, all targeted attacks and spells against the caster lose dice equal to cast successes. The effect is broken if the caster attacks or casts. Can be maintained through movement. Upkeep: 1. Shadows gather around the caster. They are harder to see. Harder to target. Shade can now obscure multiple zones and begin to corrode living targets over time. Default Ability: Lingering Dark (Permanent) Darkness from your Shade spells can only be dispelled by Bright Magic that exceeds your cast successes.

Mana Cost: 3 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, Shade, Living Range: Targeted Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Shade dots Effect: A lance of dense shadow drives into a living target. Only damages living targets. On a hit deals damage equal to excess successes. The nature of the wound makes it resist recovery: the next PHP the target receives this scene is reduced by the excess successes of this attack. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. Shadow that leaves a mark harder to heal than ordinary wounds.

Mana Cost: 3 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Persistent, Shade Range: Zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Shade dots Effect: Thick supernatural darkness fills the zone. All ranged attacks and targeted spells from or aimed at targets inside the zone lose dice equal to cast successes. Living enemies in the zone must roll Composure + Insight vs cast successes at their Upkeep Phase or lose 1 mana. Undead allies in the zone gain bonus dice equal to cast successes on all attack rolls. Bright Magic that meets or exceeds the cast successes dispels it. Upkeep: 2. The darkness fills the zone and stays. The living find it draining. Shade can now lock down mana recovery through Ethereal Shade and begin striking from ambush. Default Ability: Veil (Attuned: holds 2 of your M/T while active) While you are in a Dimmed or Darkened zone, you gain bonus dice equal to your Shade dots on Stealth rolls.

Mana Cost: 4 Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Drain, Persistent, Shade, Living Range: Targeted Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Shade dots Effect: A layer of shadow energy locks onto a living target, suppressing their mana recovery. While active, the target's mana recovery is fixed at their base rate only, with no bonus for taking damage. The target cannot recover bonus mana through any means except direct Mana Transfer while this effect is active. Additionally, the target loses mana equal to half the cast successes (rounded up) each Upkeep Phase. Bright Magic applied to the target ends the effect. Defend: Fortitude + Endurance. Upkeep: 3. A layer of shadow that limits how fast a living target can recover magic.

Mana Cost: 4 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Shade Range: Any zone in darkness or shadow within line of sight Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Shade dots Effect: The caster steps through shadow, teleporting instantly to any zone within line of sight that is Dimmed, Darkened, or occupied by a shadow-based effect (Fog of Dread, Shadow Cloak, etc.). On 3+ successes, the caster arrives unseen for their first action from the new position (they may make one attack before being locatable by sight). Zones in full daylight without any shadow cannot be targeted. Where there is shadow, the caster can be. Shade can now drain large amounts of mana directly and animate undead targets as temporary allies. Default Ability: Grave Whisper (3 mana, Instant) Touch a corpse and ask it one question. It answers with what it knew in life, in as few words as possible.

Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, Drain, AoE, Shade, Living Range: Zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Shade dots Effect: Shadow energy sweeps through a zone, draining mana from every living target in it. Caster rolls once. Every living target in the zone must resist separately. For each target, excess successes determine how much mana is drained from their pool. Undead targets in the zone are unaffected. Defend: Fortitude + Endurance. Shadow that reaches all living targets in a zone at once.

Mana Cost: 5 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Shade Range: Touch Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Shade dots Effect: The caster channels Shade energy into a recently deceased body (died within the last scene). The corpse rises as an undead under the caster's command for the rest of the scene. The animated corpse uses the base physical statistics of the deceased, with no magical abilities. It can attack in melee using the caster's Shade dice pool. It has a Vitality pool equal to cast successes. Bright Magic deals its normal undead damage to it. Upkeep: 4. Something dead gets up. It does what the caster says. Shade at this rank can corrupt the entire visible area and create permanent zones of supernatural darkness. Default Ability: Hunger (Permanent) Living targets that lose mana to your Shade spells lose 1 additional mana.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, AoE, Drain, Shade, Living Range: All zones within line of sight Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Shade dots Effect: Shadow energy expands from the caster in a pulse reaching every visible zone. Only damages living targets. Undead targets in the zones are unaffected. Caster rolls once. Every living target in every visible zone must resist separately. Each target hit takes damage equal to excess successes and loses mana equal to half those excess successes (rounded down) directly from their pool. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. Shadow goes everywhere. Everything living in sight feels it.

Mana Cost: 6 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Persistent, Shade Range: Zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Shade dots Effect: The caster presses shadow energy permanently into a zone. The zone becomes Darkened: all ranged attacks and targeted spells in or out of the zone lose dice equal to cast successes. Undead targets in the zone gain bonus dice equal to cast successes on all rolls. Bright Magic reduces cast successes by the Bright caster's successes but cannot fully dispel it unless the Bright caster's successes fully exceed the cast successes on a single cast. Upkeep: 5. The darkness becomes a permanent feature of the zone. Shade at this rank can eclipse an entire area or begin to unmake the living world. Default Ability: Umbral Form (Attuned: holds 4 of your M/T while active) Your body becomes partly shadow. While you are in a Dimmed or Darkened zone, attacks and targeted spells against you lose dice equal to your Shade dots.

Mana Cost: 7 Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, Persistent, Shade Range: All zones within line of sight Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Shade dots Effect: Every visible zone is plunged into absolute supernatural darkness. All ranged attacks and targeted spells anywhere in the area automatically lose dice equal to cast successes. All undead targets in the area gain cast successes as bonus dice on all rolls. All living targets must roll Fortitude + Endurance vs cast successes each Upkeep Phase or lose mana equal to excess successes. The Eclipse persists until the upkeep is not paid. Bright Magic that fully matches the cast successes in a single roll dispels it. Upkeep: 6. The area goes dark. Not dim. Dark. The kind of dark that drains.

Mana Cost: 7 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, Drain, Shade, Living Range: Targeted Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Shade dots Effect: A focused beam of shadow energy drives into a living target and pulls. Only damages living targets. On a hit deals damage equal to excess successes and drains mana equal to triple the excess successes directly from the target's pool. Additionally, the target must roll Fortitude + Endurance vs cast successes or lose access to their mana pool for 1 turn (they cannot spend or recover mana). Defend: Fortitude + Endurance. Willpower can be spent to resist the mana lockout: 1 Willpower negates it entirely. Shadow that reaches into a living target and pulls out more than mana.

Every combination spell states the minimum dots required in each school. The dot cap is the lowest rating among all schools involved. If you have 5 dots in Fire but only 2 in Earth, a Fire plus Earth combination is capped as though both schools were at 2. The combination spell's rank cannot exceed that cap regardless of individual school ratings.

A combination spell can be taken for free when gaining a new dot in one of its required schools, if that dot satisfies the prerequisites. Instead of taking one of the two standard options for that dot, the player takes the combination spell. This is the only way to learn a combination spell for free. Otherwise a combination spell costs Rank x2 XP for each school it combines, where Rank is the dots it requires in each school.

A combination spell costs mana equal to the total dots it requires: the number of schools multiplied by the dots required in each. A two-school spell requires 2 dots in each school, 4 dots in all, and costs 4 mana. A three-school spell requires 3 dots in each, 9 in all, and costs 9 mana. Upkeep is always the mana cost minus 1.

s: Combination Spells in Artifacts and Implements
t: A combination spell imbued in an artifact or implement does not require the user to meet dot prerequisites. The item is treated as having the required dots built into it. The user simply provides the mana.

Creation Magic is the single combination of all seven casting schools at 7 dots each. It is the only way to bring new autonomous life into the world, and it can be the work of many people together. Its full rules are at the end of this part.
Prerequisite: 2 dots in each school. Mana cost: 4. Upkeep: 3.

Prerequisite: 2 dots Water, 2 dots Nature Mana Cost: 4 Upcast: 2 mana per additional die or effect Upkeep: 3 Speed: Instant Type: Attack, Persistent, CC Range: Targeted Dice Pool: Dexterity + Magic + Water dots + Nature dots (cap at lowest) Effect: Water-fed vines erupt from the ground and constrict a target. Target is Rooted. Each Upkeep Phase the target remains Rooted they take damage equal to the original attack successes. The target can attempt to break free by rolling Strength + Athletics against the original cast successes during their Upkeep Phase. Living vines fed by flowing water seize the target and squeeze.

Prerequisite: 2 dots Earth, 2 dots Shade Mana Cost: 4 Upcast: 2 mana per additional die or effect Upkeep: 3 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Persistent, Drain, Corrupt, Buff Range: Zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + Earth dots + Shade dots (cap at lowest) Effect: Living targets in the zone must roll Fortitude + Endurance vs cast successes each Upkeep Phase or lose mana equal to the excess successes. Undead targets in the zone gain bonus dice equal to caster successes on attack rolls. Bright Magic applied to the zone dispels it. Dark energy seeps up through the earth, corrupting the ground itself.

Radiant steam that burns conditions away from allies and forces undead out.

Prerequisite: 3 dots Fire, 3 dots Air, 3 dots Nature Mana Cost: 9 Upcast: 3 mana per additional die or effect Upkeep: N/A Speed: Instant Type: Attack, AoE Range: AoE-4 (2x2 zone area) Dice Pool: Attribute + Magic + lowest dots among combined schools Effect: Floating spores drift to a 2x2 zone area and detonate on arrival. Prerequisite: 3 dots Air, 3 dots Nature, 3 dots Bright Mana Cost: 9 Upcast: 3 mana per additional die or effect Upkeep: 8 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Persistent, Healing, CC Range: Zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + lowest dots among combined schools Effect: Luminescent spores fill the zone. Undead targets in the zone must pass the same roll or gain Exhausted. Shade Magic dispels it. Glowing spores that mend allies and disorient everyone else.

Prerequisite: 3 dots Water, 3 dots Earth, 3 dots Nature Mana Cost: 9 Upcast: 3 mana per additional die or effect Upkeep: 8 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Persistent, CC Range: Zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + lowest dots among combined schools Effect: Dense waterlogged terrain choked with plant growth fills the zone. Prerequisite: 3 dots Fire, 3 dots Water, 3 dots Earth Mana Cost: 9 Upcast: 3 mana per additional die or effect Upkeep: 8 Speed: Instant Type: Utility, Persistent, CC, Attack Range: Zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + lowest dots among combined schools Effect: Superheated water is forced through cracked earth, erupting as scalding geysers across the zone. Each target defends separately against the same attack successes. Targets hit take damage equal to excess successes. Undead targets take double damage. Paying the upkeep during the Upkeep Phase freezes the countdown for that turn. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. Heat to soften, weight to hold, and two opposite forces to seal it shut.

The pool lasts until the end of the target's next turn, and any unused points are lost. Countdown: lasts turns equal to half the mana spent, rounded up. Paying the upkeep during the Upkeep Phase freezes the countdown for that turn. Rain that feels like a hearth after a long night.

Every target in the line defends separately. Targets hit take damage equal to excess successes and gain the Burning condition. Every zone in the line becomes difficult terrain from the glassed ground. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. Where the lightning ran, the ground turned to glass.

Prerequisite: 4 dots Air, 4 dots Earth, 4 dots Bright, 4 dots Shade Mana Cost: 16 Upcast: 4 mana per additional die or effect Upkeep: 15 Speed: Instant, Extended Type: Utility, CC, Persistent Range: Targeted (object or creature in line of sight) Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + lowest dots among combined schools Effect: The caster takes complete control of a target's relationship to gravity, increasing or decreasing it in either direction by factors. The caster chooses direction and intensity at cast time. Each success on the roll increases the factor by 1 in either direction. At 1 success: weight is halved or doubled. At 3 successes: weight is quartered or quadrupled. At 5 successes: target is weightless (floats freely without wind) or crushed (takes 1 damage each Upkeep Phase from compression and cannot move on their own). At 7+ successes: the target can be projected upward as if launched (weightless + upward velocity) or collapsed inward under extreme gravity (Pinned condition, 2 damage each Upkeep Phase). Countdown: lasts turns equal to half the mana spent, rounded up. Paying the upkeep during the Upkeep Phase freezes the countdown for that turn. Resist: Fortitude + Endurance. Increasing successes in the crushing direction requires re-rolling each turn at the same cost. Bright and Shade together can regulate fundamental forces when guided by Earth and Air. What they can do to weight in either direction is a matter of how many successes the caster can bring to it.

All zones in the area become difficult terrain from the broken shards. Defend: Dexterity + Dodge. Four elements melt, fire, and shatter into a single scouring storm.

Creation Magic is the single combination of all seven casting schools. It is a miracle. It is the only magic in Terrana that brings something genuinely new into existence: a being with a will of its own, a material that has never existed, a thing that remains when the magic is gone. Prerequisite: 7 dots in Fire, Water, Air, Earth, Nature, Bright, and Shade for a single caster Mana Cost: 49 Upcast: 7 mana per additional die or effect Upkeep: N/A (what it creates is permanent) Speed: Instant for a single caster, or gathered over time Type: Creation Range: Touch or adjacent zone Dice Pool: Intelligence + Magic + lowest dots among combined schools

Creation Magic does not have to come from one caster, and it does not have to be paid all at once. Throughout history it has manifested through the combined efforts of many people. A circle of mages might each play their part, one shaping the body, another the mind, another the spark that holds it together. Their mana and will build toward the same creation until it is complete. It does not always happen on purpose. Thousands of years ago, the people of a town believed a god lived in the mountain beside them. Generation after generation, their prayers, their belief, and the ambient magic of the land gathered in that mountain until the god they imagined manifested and took up residence there. It lives there still.

Creation Magic answers whatever is poured into it. It has made benevolent beings who protect the people who imagined them, and it has made evil ones. Every daemon in existence was given life by the combined fears of people. What a people dread long enough and deeply enough can become real.

A conjuration is mana shaped into a temporary form. It needs upkeep, it ends when the upkeep stops or the caster is Incapacitated, and it can be dispelled. Creation Magic is different. What it makes exists on its own the moment it is complete. It needs no upkeep, it does not end when its creators fall, and it cannot be dispelled, because it is no longer a spell. It is part of the world.

Creation Magic is the only way to make fully autonomous life. Soul Summoning can create an entity that follows its summoner's commands, but that entity has no will of its own. A being made through Creation Magic thinks, chooses, and acts for itself. A created being is not bound to obey those who made it. Anyone who wants its help has to earn it, ask for it, or make a pact with it, the same as with any other autonomous being. A created being can learn and use all seven casting schools, combination magic, and anything else a person can learn. The player and the Storyteller build a created being together as a new character.

The successes behind a creation set how complex it can be: 1 to 2 successes: a simple object, material, or plant life 3 to 4 successes: a living creature with animal instincts but no will beyond them 5 to 6 successes: an autonomous being with its own mind and will 7 or more successes: an autonomous being of significant power, or a material with properties never seen before

Resurrection is a separate spell (see Resurrection). Creation Magic makes something new rather than restoring what was lost. Circle magic covers all ritual-based magical disciplines that operate outside the seven casting schools and Battle Aura. The defining rule is that circle magic cannot be used in combat. The preparation required cannot be compressed into the turn structure without losing what makes it work. A finished circle magic item, scroll, or contract can be used at any time, including in combat. A devil carrying a pre-signed contract into a negotiation can activate it during social combat. A scroll prepared before the encounter can be read aloud during the fight. The restriction applies to the creation and preparation of circle magic, not to the use of a finished product.

Circle magic covers all ritual-based magical disciplines that operate outside the seven casting schools and Battle Aura. The defining rule is that circle magic cannot be used in combat. The preparation required cannot be compressed into the turn structure without losing what makes it work. A finished circle magic item, scroll, or contract can be used at any time, including in combat. A devil carrying a pre-signed contract into a negotiation can activate it during social combat. A scroll prepared before the encounter can be read aloud during the fight. The restriction applies to the creation and preparation of circle magic, not to the use of a finished product.

Circle magic disciplines appear under Magical Knowledges on the character sheet alongside the seven casting schools. They follow the same XP cost structure. They do not follow the same seven-rank spell list format. Each discipline has its own rules for what the practitioner can accomplish at different dot ratings, and those rules are listed under each discipline's entry.

Circle Magic is not a school of direct casting. It is a meta-discipline - a body of knowledge that allows a practitioner to capture, store, transfer, and reshape magical effects that other schools produce. A mage with Circle Magic dots can write what they know into the world in ways that persist beyond their own attention, and can interact with phenomena that raw casting cannot reach. Circle Magic replaces the Magic ability in any Circle Magic roll. Where a casting school uses Intelligence + Magic + school dots, a circle of that spell uses Intelligence + Circle Magic + school dots. A Circle Magic roll that does not draw on a casting school uses Intelligence + Circle Magic. The successes from that roll are committed at the moment the circle or scroll or contract is made. They do not change after creation. Circle Magic is learned separately from casting schools and has its own dot progression on the character sheet. A character does not need to know any particular school to study Circle Magic, but many of its disciplines only become truly powerful when combined with a deep knowledge of other schools. The disciplines below represent the major branches of study within Circle Magic. A practitioner may pursue any combination of them. Some practitioners specialize deeply in one form; others take a broader approach.

Scroll Magic is the foundational discipline of Circle Magic and the one most practitioners learn first. A scroll is a prepared vessel for a single spell, committed at creation and released later by anyone who can provide the mana.

To create a scroll, the caster must know the spell they wish to encode and have at least as many Circle Magic dots as the spell's rank. They draw the appropriate circle on a suitable medium - paper, cloth, stone, skin - channeling both the spell's school and the Circle Magic framework simultaneously. The caster rolls Intelligence + Circle Magic + the spell's school dots. The successes achieved are locked into the scroll at creation. These successes serve as the spell's outcome when the scroll is later released. The caster does not roll again at release. For damage spells, the scroll's creator writes the damage type and notes the success count on the scroll itself. Mana cost at creation: the creator spends the spell's full mana cost at the time of creation, plus 1 additional mana per Circle Magic dot involved as the framework cost.

Anyone holding a scroll can release it by spending the spell's mana cost from their own pool. They do not need to know the spell's school. The scroll activates using the success count locked in at creation. The scroll is consumed upon release. A scroll cannot be released in the same turn it is drawn out. Drawing a scroll takes a standard action. Releasing it takes a standard action on the following turn.

A character can carry prepared scrolls equal to their Circle Magic dots. Scrolls kept in inventory beyond combat reach take no limit slot. A scroll created by someone else functions normally. Scrolls degrade after one month if not stored in a proper Circle Satchel (a minor magical item worth noting on equipment lists).
Divination uses Circle Magic to read information from time, place, and connection rather than imposing effects on the world. A diviner asks questions of the fabric of things.

With 1-2 Circle Magic dots, a practitioner can read recent impressions from objects and places. Roll Intelligence + Circle Magic. Each success reveals one fact about the most recent significant event tied to the object or location. The scene is the minimum time frame; exact timing requires more successes.

With 3-5 dots, a practitioner can trace connections between people and objects across distances. They can ask directional questions (which way, how far) or temporal ones (when did this happen, how long ago). The difficulty scales with distance and time elapsed. A question about something that happened yesterday in the same city is trivial. A question about something that happened three decades ago in another country requires a very high success count.

With 6-7 dots, a practitioner can look forward. Future divination is never exact. The GM provides images, sensations, and symbolic impressions rather than facts. Probability is not certainty, and the future shifts based on choices made. What a 6-dot diviner sees is the most likely outcome from the current moment forward; a 7-dot diviner sees several branching paths and their relative likelihood. Neither sees inevitability. Future divination costs 5 mana per attempt and requires at least 30 uninterrupted minutes outside of combat.
Summoning Magic brings entities from other planes or states of being into the physical world. It is divided into two branches with different prerequisites, rules, and risks.

Fiend Summoning calls creatures that already exist in the world. A summoner gains a fiend by catching it, making a pact with it, or buying it. When a fiend is not needed it lives in a ranch or another place where it can live happily. Each fiend is tied to a device etched with its soul mark. The summoner carries that device and uses it to call the fiend to the battlefield from wherever it is in the world. The device can take any form, such as a ball or a coin. In the current day it is most popular to keep them on cards, and fiends are bought, sold, and traded this way. In common use these creatures are called SumMonz. Fiends can use the five main elemental casting schools (Fire, Water, Air, Earth, and Nature) and Battle Aura.

Soul Summoning covers beings that do not fall into the fiend category. These beings live in a demi-plane or a similar place and are summoned from there. They include fey beings, undead creatures, devils, and even a completely new being of the player's own design. A summoner can make a pact with an existing being that already has its own autonomy, such as a fey or a devil. A summoner can also create an entity of their own. Without Creation Magic that entity is not fully autonomous life. It is an entity that follows the summoner's commands. Soul summoned beings can use all seven casting schools, including combination magic. This is the main system difference between the two branches of summoning.

Most people, even those in the SumMonz League, do not know or care about the distinction between fiends and soul summoned beings. What they do care about is that elemental creatures are affected differently by elemental attacks. A water sprite deals more damage to a fire sprite, and so on, following the Elemental Advantages.

Cards in Combat: Circle magic cannot be started in combat, but a card etched with a soul mark is a finished product, so you can summon from one mid-fight. Without the card you cannot summon that SumMonz. Summoning: During either Move or Use Item phase, spend mana equal to the SumMonz's rank to call it to an empty zone next to you. It counts as using a belt item and follows the same AP costs. Calling it back to its card is free. How Many: You can have 1 SumMonz on the field at 1 to 3 dots of Summoning Magic, 2 at 4 to 6 dots, and 3 at 7. You can carry up to 6 cards at once. Where They Live: Fiends you are not carrying live at a ranch or another place where they can live happily. Soul summoned beings live in the Dreeming or the Seeming and are called from there. Commanding: A summoned SumMonz acts on your turn, and commanding it costs you no action. It moves and attacks in the same phases you do, using its own pools. Support: You can give your SumMonz AP and mana the same way you would give them to an ally, and any healing that works on a character works on a SumMonz. Rank Limit: A SumMonz's rank can never be raised above your Summoning Magic dots. One that outranks you, such as a gift or a fiend whose summoner died, may refuse commands. A Composure + Summoning Magic roll against its rank x2 brings it in line for the scene. Knocked Out: A SumMonz that is Incapacitated returns to its card and cannot be summoned again until after a long rest. Elements: Elemental Advantages apply to SumMonz exactly as they do to spells and conjurations.

Every SumMonz is built from its rank (R), from 1 at F to 7 at S, using the same numbers as every creature in the Bestiary ( Chapter 15 ). Attack and Defense: 2R + 2 dice each. Damage: a damage pool of R + 2 dice, rolled like a weapon's. Add the attack's excess successes and compare the total to the target's thresholds. Thresholds: BDT R + 2, LDT BDT x2, ADT BDT x3. Health: R + 2 Bashing boxes, R + 1 Lethal boxes, and R Aggravated boxes. Mana: Pool 3R, M/T R + 1. A SumMonz pays for its own techniques from its own pool. Movement: 1 zone per turn. A flying SumMonz moves at double. Techniques: Up to 4, chosen from spells of a rank no higher than its own, rolled with its own Attack pool. Fiends draw from Fire, Water, Air, Earth, and Nature Magic and Battle Aura. Soul summoned beings draw from all seven casting schools and combination magic.

While a SumMonz is on the field, you can pour more mana into it to push it into a stronger form. This counts toward your Max Mana Per Turn, and an evolved form may rise above your Summoning Magic dots while it lasts. Second Form: Spend mana equal to the second form's rank. The SumMonz rises 1 rank, its stats rise to match, and it gains its form technique. Third Form: From its second form, spend mana equal to the third form's rank. It rises another rank, grows to fill a 2x2 zone area, and gains its third form technique. Holding a Form: An evolved form burns its own mana each Upkeep Phase: 1 for the second form, 2 for the third. When its mana runs out, it reverts to its first form. If you call it back and do not summon it again within 2 turns, it also reverts.

Catching: Weaken a wild fiend until all of its Lethal boxes are filled, then press a blank card to it and roll Wisdom + Summoning Magic against its rank x2. On a success its soul mark is etched into the card. Blank cards are sold by rank and priced like any item of that rank ( Chapter 14 ). Pacts: A fiend or soul summoned being that can talk may agree to a pact instead. Play it out as a social scene, usually Persuasion or Diplomacy against its Composure. It will want something in return. Buying and Trading: SumMonz cards are bought, sold, and traded like any item of their rank ( Chapter 14 ). Whoever holds the card holds the SumMonz. Growing: Raise a SumMonz's rank by spending XP equal to the new rank x3, never above your Summoning Magic dots. Each new rank can add one technique, up to 4. Creating: A soul summoned being of your own design starts at rank 1 and grows the same way. Without Creation Magic it follows your commands but has no will of its own. Example: Cinder is an Ember Fox fiend (Fire and Battle Aura) of rank D (3): Attack 8, Defense 8, Damage 5, BDT 5, Health 5 / 4 / 3, Mana 9, M/T 4, Movement 1. Summoning Cinder costs 3 mana. Pouring in 4 more evolves it into Blazetail (rank 4), and 5 more after that into Pyre Vixen (rank 5), who fills a 2x2 area. Summoner's Sheet: Track up to 6 SumMonz, with all three forms, on the Summoner's Sheet at the back of this book.

Teleportation Magic uses circles drawn at both origin and destination to create an instantaneous passage between two prepared points. Unlike Shadow Step (which uses existing darkness), Teleportation Magic creates its own passage.

The standard use of Teleportation requires the caster to have previously prepared a destination circle and have it active. A destination circle takes 10 minutes to inscribe, costs Circle Magic dots in mana, and persists for up to a month without maintenance. The caster keeps a resonance token - a small inscribed object - that lets them call the circle when opening the transit. Activating a transit: roll Intelligence + Circle Magic. The transit opens on 1 success and remains open for 1 turn per success, allowing any number of willing travelers to pass through. The mana cost is 2 per Circle Magic dot. A caster may only have active destination circles equal to their Circle Magic dots at one time.

With 5+ Circle Magic dots, a caster can force a teleportation without a prepared destination circle, selecting any location they have personally visited and can visualize clearly. This is harder: the roll loses 2 dice, the mana cost doubles, and the transit only allows one traveler (the caster). On a failure, the teleportation does not occur and the mana is spent. On a botch (all dice fail), the transit occurs but deposits the caster somewhere adjacent to rather than at the intended destination.

Teleporting to a location one has never seen requires a combination of Divination and Teleportation (minimum 5 dots in Circle Magic and at least 1 success on a prior Divination roll about the location). This is extremely difficult and the margin for error is significant. This is the purview of the most experienced practitioners only.

Contract Magic makes binding agreements - magical compacts with real teeth. A contract created through Circle Magic is enforced not by trust but by force. The moment both parties sign or otherwise accept the terms, the magic takes hold.

A Circle Magic practitioner draws up a contract by scribing its terms within a circle. The terms must be specific and possible to verify. Vague language works against the writer: the magic interprets terms literally, and ambiguity is resolved against the party who drafted the contract. The caster rolls Intelligence + Circle Magic to set the contract's power level. More successes mean a tighter binding with harsher consequences for breach. A contract must specify: the parties involved, the terms each party agrees to, the duration, and the consequence for breach. The consequence for breach must be proportionate in some form - a contract cannot specify death for a minor obligation, though what counts as proportionate is a matter for the GM and the players to navigate.

A contract activates the moment all named parties have accepted its terms. Acceptance can be a signature, a spoken agreement in the circle's presence, or any other clear act of consent. Coerced signatures are valid but contested: a party who signed under direct magical compulsion may challenge the contract before a higher power (a guild, a court, a more powerful Circle mage). Once activated, the contract is a persistent magical effect. Both parties feel its presence as a faint but unmistakable sensation whenever they take an action that might be relevant to the terms.

If a party breaches the terms of an active contract, the magic triggers. Mild contracts impose conditions (Disadvantaged on relevant rolls, recurring minor damage). Strong contracts (created by high-success casters) can be genuinely dangerous - the breaching party may take Lethal or even Aggravated damage, lose mana, or suffer persistent conditions until the breach is resolved. The magic does not care about intent; it cares about the letter of the terms. A contract can be dissolved by mutual consent of all parties. It can also be broken by destroying the physical medium on which it was written, though this requires more successes on a Circle Magic roll than were used to create it.

Devil contracts are a specific and particularly binding form of Contract Magic. A contract with a devil follows all the rules above but adds several complications. Devils negotiate their terms very carefully and always seek the version of events most favorable to their interpretation. They will not sign a contract they cannot fulfill, but they will sign contracts designed to make fulfillment advantageous on their terms. A devil that breaches its contract suffers consequences in proportion to the breach, as with any contract, but these consequences extend to their standing in their home plane. Devils take contract obligations seriously for this reason. A human party that breaches a devil contract typically suffers worse consequences than a comparable mundane contract would impose, because devils draft their contracts with that asymmetry built in. Reading every clause carefully before signing is not just good advice - it is a survival skill.

Binding Rituals use Circle Magic to affix magical effects, spirits, or entities to objects, locations, or thresholds. Unlike contracts, bindings do not require consent from the target. They are imposed by force or prepared in advance.

An object can be bound with any spell effect the caster knows. The object stores the effect until a trigger condition is met. The trigger must be specific and detectable: "when touched by a person not carrying my resonance token," "when this seal is broken," "when someone speaks the word carved on the lid." Abstract triggers do not work. Binding an effect to an object requires the caster to have both the spell and at least Circle Magic dots equal to the spell's rank. They cast the spell into the object rather than into the world, rolling Intelligence + Circle Magic + the spell's school dots. The successes are stored with the binding. The bound effect can trigger once (expendable binding) or repeatedly at the cost of a mana charge per trigger (persistent binding, which requires the object to have a mana reservoir).

A location can be bound with effects that trigger on entry, exit, or condition. Location bindings are used to create traps, wards, and persistent environmental effects. A Zone-scale location binding covers one zone. Larger areas require higher Circle Magic dots and proportionally more successes. Location bindings persist for a month per Circle Magic dot used in the creation. A permanent location binding requires at least 6 Circle Magic dots and a very high success count. Permanent bindings are rare and usually notable features of the places that contain them.

Entity binding captures an entity and forces it into an object or location. It requires a contest between the binder's Circle Magic roll and the entity's resistance and costs 5 mana per Circle Magic dot. Once bound, the entity is contained. It is aware of its imprisonment. It retains its personality and goals. This is worth remembering when dealing with pacted creatures who were bound rather than persuaded.

Wards are protective or alerting circles placed on zones, objects, or thresholds. They are a specialized subset of location bindings focused specifically on detecting intrusion, deflecting effects, or creating contained areas of magical influence.

An alert ward triggers silently and notifies the creator when a condition is met. The notification is a mental impression - a directional sense of activation, the general nature of what triggered it, and a rough sense of distance. Alert wards do not require high success counts; even 1 success on the creation roll produces a functional ward. Higher successes give more precise information on trigger. Alert wards cost 1 mana per Circle Magic dot to create and persist for a week per success.

A defensive ward interposes itself between a protected zone or object and incoming magical effects. When a spell targets something inside a defensive ward, the ward's creation successes act as a resistance DT against that spell. The ward absorbs hits by losing successes; when reduced to 0, it breaks. Defensive wards cost 3 mana per Circle Magic dot to create. They persist until broken or until a month has passed. They can be recharged by spending mana equal to their original creation cost, which restores their success pool.

An exclusion ward creates an invisible line that certain types of entities or effects cannot cross. A ward against undead, against fey, against fire effects, or against a specific named entity requires the caster to have at least as many Circle Magic dots as the category's power level. Low-level undead can be warded off by a 2-dot exclusion; a named ancient vampire requires 6+. Exclusion wards do not damage entities; they simply prevent passage. A powerful enough entity can push through an exclusion ward by spending Willpower and succeeding on a contested roll against the ward's creation successes.

Augmentation is the circle magic of building magic into weapons so that their attacks can carry it. A weapon can only receive an augmentation if its description lists an augment slot. An augmentation can be made from any of the seven casting magics, or even from other circle magics. Using an augmentation during an attack still requires spending mana. Each augmentation has its own parameters, set when it is made, that determine what it can and cannot do. An augmented attack follows the same mana assignment rules as any attack carrying a school's energy (see Imbuing Attacks).

Spatial Magic folds space so that a container holds far more than its outside size should allow. It is used most often to make magical storage implements: bags, chests, pouches, rings, and similar items. Storage is counted per kind of object. The strength of the design, set by the Circle Magic dots put into it, decides how many of each kind of object it can hold. Each dot doubles the amount: 1 dot: 1 of each kind of object 2 dots: 2 of each kind of object 3 dots: 4 of each kind of object 4 dots: 8 of each kind of object 5 dots: 16 of each kind of object 6 dots: 32 of each kind of object 7 dots: 64 of each kind of object A storage implement made at 3 dots can hold 4 swords, 4 potions, 4 loaves of bread, and 4 of every other kind of object at the same time. The creator chooses the strength of the design, up to their own Circle Magic dots.

Time Magic is the deepest and most demanding branch of Circle Magic. It is not fully expressible within the conventional dot scale, and serious time magic lies beyond what any practitioner currently active has reliably achieved. However, it is an area of active study, and the foundations are accessible.

A practitioner with 4-5 Circle Magic dots can produce minor temporal effects: slowing or accelerating the passage of time within a small object (aging a fruit, preserving a body, slowing the burning of a candle). These effects do not affect living creatures and do not change the past or future. They manipulate the rate at which time passes for inert things within a prepared circle.

At 6 Circle Magic dots, a practitioner can create a Temporal Stasis circle that suspends time within a small zone or object entirely. Anything inside the circle stops aging, stops changing, stops experiencing duration. The effect persists until the circle is broken. This is used to preserve things perfectly: wounds, artifacts, living creatures placed voluntarily inside. A creature placed in stasis does not experience the time that passes while stasis is active. Temporal Stasis cost: 10 mana to create, 2 mana per day to maintain for a persistent circle. Breaking a stasis circle (from outside) requires meeting or exceeding its creation successes on a Circle Magic roll.

At 7 Circle Magic dots, a practitioner can observe the past of a specific location - not through Divination's impressions, but through direct temporal viewing. They see events as they occurred, with clarity proportional to success count and proximity to the present. One success per decade of distance is the rough scale. Temporal Observation cannot change the past. It does not allow communication with the past. It is purely a window. The practitioner sees and hears; they cannot interact.

The ability to directly alter past events, travel through time, or bring future states into the present is theoretically within the reach of Circle Magic but lies beyond the standard dot scale. Whether such a thing is truly possible - and what it would cost - remains one of the open questions in the magical world. Practitioners who pursue this path report that the circles required are of extraordinary complexity, the mana costs staggering, and the philosophical implications not easily survived. If a player wishes to pursue time travel as a long-term goal for their character, discuss with your GM. It is a valid aspiration. The path to it is not charted here because it has not yet been charted at all.

No circle magic can be initiated during combat. Any technique that requires setup, preparation, drawn lines, or spoken incantation taking longer than one instant cannot be started once initiative has been called. A practitioner who was mid-ritual when combat begins has their ritual interrupted unless the Storyteller rules otherwise. The exception is finished products. A scroll, contract, ward trigger, or bound item that was completed before the fight started can be activated as normal. Activating a finished product follows the product's own rules for speed and cost, not the rules for ritual preparation.

Gear does not make the adventurer, but it helps. This chapter covers what things cost, what you can carry into a fight, the weapons and armor of modern Terrana, the everyday tools and magic that fill a delver's pack, and the tables a Storyteller rolls on when a party finds something worth keeping. The weapons and prices here describe modern Terrana. Games set in the distant past, a fallen future, or the space era change what is available and what it costs ( Chapter 16 ).

Monsera's influence has standardized currency across the major trade routes. Coins are the everyday money of Terrana, and mana crystals of matching value change hands just as freely, since every implement in the world runs on them. The values in our world's dollars are only a guide for the table.

Money on hand is tracked separately: write your current funds next to Resources on your sheet and keep it up to date as you earn and spend.

Starting Funds is the money your character has when play begins. Poor (0 dots) is here for examples and for alternate era games. Every weapon, piece of armor, tool, and magic item has a Rating from 1 to 7, matching the same F through S ranks used everywhere else. A Rating adds to the rolls the item is made for: a weapon's Rating adds to its damage, armor's Rating adds to your BDT, and a set of lockpicks adds its Rating to Sleight of Hand rolls to open a lock. Weapons and Armor: A weapon or a piece of armor gets its Rating from its rank alone: F rank is +1, E is +2, D is +3, C is +4, B is +5, A is +6, and S is +7. A rusty F rank greatsword and an F rank dagger both add 1 to damage; what makes the greatsword different is its damage Attribute, its properties, and the Style it uses. Ordinary store-bought weapons and armor are usually F or E rank. A rank and S rank pieces are true masterworks, rarely seen and almost never for sale. Other Items: Tools, rings, and other gear also have a rank, but their bonuses are usually smaller than a weapon's, as listed in their entries and on the loot tables.

Rating Rank Typical Price Example 1 F 2 to 9 Large Copper A plain knife or a store-bought sword, a bedroll 2 E 1 to 9 Small Silver A well-made weapon, a leather jacket, a climbing kit 3 D 1 to 9 Large Silver A fine weapon, a chain shirt, a CCN crystal 4 C 1 to 9 Small Gold An expert's weapon, tactical armor, a minor magic ring 5 B 1 to 9 Large Gold A master's weapon, full plate, a crystal-engine car 6 A 1 to 9 King's Gold A famous blade, enchanted plate, a small airship 7 S Rarely for sale Legendary arms, unique artifacts

Equipment Slots: Your sheet has a slot for each place you can wear or hold something: Headgear, Torso, Left Arm, Right Arm, Legs, Footwear, Main Weapon, Side Arm, Alt Weapons, and Stowed Items. Gloves, bracers, and rings go on the arm they are worn on; paired items go on both arms. Weapons: You can carry at most 3 weapons and wield at most 2 at once. Swapping to an alt weapon costs 1 AP or your attack action that turn. The Belt: Before combat, set up to 3 items on your belt for quick use. The first belt item you use in a turn is free, the second costs 1 AP, and the third costs 2 more AP, so using all three in one turn costs 3 AP. Items are used during the Move or Use Item phases; moving and using an item in the same phase costs AP. Belt Slots 4 to 7: Extra belt slots open only when an item or ability grants them, such as Quickcut's Hidden Steel or Windreader's Quiver Belt, each of which opens slot 4 for one kind of item. Stowed Items: Anything not worn, wielded, or on your belt is stowed. Retrieving a stowed item costs 1 AP or your attack action.

Attack: Your attack roll is the Attribute + Ability + Combat Style listed for the weapon's Style ( Chapter 12 ). Without the Style, roll the Attribute + Ability alone. Damage: Your damage pool is the weapon's damage Attribute + its Rating, which comes from its rank (+1 at F up to +7 at S). Add the attack's excess successes and compare the total to the target's BDT, LDT, and ADT. Damage Attribute: Each weapon lists the Attribute that drives its damage. Most use Strength or Dexterity, and firearms and bows use Perception, but some weapons use another Attribute entirely: a whip that works by trickery might use Manipulation, and a focus weapon might use Intelligence. Range: Melee weapons hit adjacent zones, or one zone farther with the Reach property. Thrown weapons and objects can be thrown accurately up to double your Strength in zones, fewer for large or heavy things (Storyteller's call). Bows, guns, and ranged spells have no set range: they can hit anywhere on the battlefield you have line of sight to. Line of Sight and Cover: Draw a straight line from the center of your square to the center of the target's square. If it passes through both the front and the back of the square the target is hiding behind, the target has full cover and cannot be hit. If it only crosses a side and the back of that square, or a corner, the target has half cover: -2 dice to the attack. Otherwise the shot is clear. AP: Most weapons attack with your normal attack action. A weapon with an AP cost needs that much AP spent on top of the attack.

Concealable: Small enough to hide easily. +2 dice to keep it hidden when searched. Light: Can be wielded in your off hand alongside another weapon. Loud: Firing it gives away your position, even if you are hidden. Mounted: Must be braced, set on a stand, or fired from a vehicle. You cannot move in a turn you fire it. Reload (X): After X attacks, spend 1 AP or your attack action to reload. Reach: Can hit a target one zone farther than adjacent. Thrown: Can be thrown up to double your Strength in zones, using the Style's Primary pool. Two-Handed: Needs both hands. You cannot hold a shield or a second weapon. Only armor worn on the body and the head adds to your Armor, and your Armor is added to your BDT (Fortitude + Armor). Arms, legs, rings, gloves, boots, and the like give other properties instead, such as bonus dice or bonus ability dots, and the most expensive pieces can even grant attribute dots. Armor Rating: Like weapons, armor gets its Rating from its rank: F +1 up to S +7. Armor Classes: The class decides which ranks a piece can come in. Light armor runs from F to D (Armor 1 to 3), Medium from D to B (3 to 5), and Heavy from B to S (5 to 7). Who Can Wear What: Your Physical column limits what you can wear. Aversion: Light armor only. Standard: Light or Medium. Affinity: any armor. The same limit applies to shields. Helmets: A helmet adds 1 Armor; a full helm adds 2, but only with Heavy body armor. Magic and Armor: Armor can be enchanted for added effects, but only rarely to add more Armor. Points added by magic count as the magic part of your BDT, which Magic Penetration can ignore.

Magic items come in two kinds: implements and artifacts. The difference is whether someone designed the magic or the world put it there.

An implement is made on purpose to produce a specific effect, usually with circle magic. Implements are part of everyday life in Terrana: microwaves, fridges, lamps that never need oil, and storage pouches made with Spatial Magic are all implements. In games set in the future or in space, replicators and similar devices are implements too. An implement does what it was designed to do. Its effect is known, repeatable, and the same every time. Using one costs mana each time, but it never needs attunement.

An artifact is an item that spent time somewhere with a high density of mana, such as a dungeon, and soaked up random magical abilities. Any item can become an artifact this way, from an ordinary object to an implement. No one designs an artifact's abilities, and two artifacts that started as the same item can end up nothing alike. Attunement: To use an artifact you must attune to it, which holds part of your Max Mana Per Turn equal to its Rating for as long as you stay attuned. Once attuned, it needs no further mana to use.

An augmentation is a magical or mechanical enhancement built into the body or into a weapon with an augment slot, made with the Augmentation circle magic ( Chapter 13 ). Body augmentations work like a natural limb while attuned and hold M/T equal to their Rating. Arcane Enhancements bought as Merits ( Chapter 9 ) work differently and lower M/T permanently.

A spell held in an implement or artifact, including a combination spell, does not require the user to meet its dot prerequisites. The item has the required dots built in; the user simply provides the mana.

When a party finds treasure, the Storyteller can choose it or roll for it. Rolling takes three steps: 1. Loot Rank: Roll a d10 on the Loot Rank table for where the party is. This sets the item's rank, F through S. 2. What You Found: Roll a d100 to see what kind of item it is. 3. Bonus: Roll a d10 on the Bonus table for the item's rank. Where a bonus says "an ability" or "an attribute," roll on the Which Ability or Which Attribute table, or pick one that fits the item. A weapon or armor gets its Rating from its rank (F +1 to S +7), and the bonus table adds something extra on top. Coin, potions, and crystals skip step 3. An item of B rank or higher, or any item found deep in a dungeon, may also roll on Artifact Quirks.
